stories.title: 📜 Revelation 1
summaryBullets: This is the revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His servants what must soon come to pass. He made it known by sending His angel to His servant John, (1:1).
who testifies to everything he saw. This is the word of God and the testimony of Jesus Christ. (1:2).
Blessed is the one who reads aloud the words of this prophecy, and blessed are those who hear and obey what is written in it, because the time is near. (1:3).
John, To the seven churches in the province of Asia: Grace and peace to you from Him who is and was and is to come, and from the seven spirits before His throne, (1:4).
and from Jesus Christ, the faithful witness, the firstborn from the dead, and the ruler of the kings of the earth. To Him who loves us and has released us from our sins by His blood, (1:5).
who has made us to be a kingdom, priests to His God and Father — to Him be the glory and power forever and ever! Amen. (1:6).
Behold, He is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see Him — even those who pierced Him. And all the tribes of the earth will mourn because of Him. So shall it be! Amen. (1:7).
“I am the Alpha and the Omega,” says the Lord God, who is and was and is to come — the Almighty. (1:8).
I, John, your brother and partner in the tribulation and kingdom and perseverance that are in Jesus, was on the island of Patmos because of the word of God and my testimony about Jesus. (1:9).
On the Lord’s day I was in the Spirit, and I heard behind me a loud voice like a trumpet, (1:10).
[J]saying,“Write on a scroll what you see and send it to the seven churches: to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea.”[/J] (1:11).
Then I turned to see the voice that was speaking with me. And having turned, I saw seven golden lampstands, (1:12).
and among the lampstands was One like the Son of Man, dressed in a long robe, with a golden sash around His chest. (1:13).
The hair of His head was white like wool, as white as snow, and His eyes were like a blazing fire. (1:14).
His feet were like polished bronze refined in a furnace, and His voice was like the roar of many waters. (1:15).
He held in His right hand seven stars, and a sharp double-edged sword came from His mouth. His face was like the sun shining at its brightest. (1:16).
When I saw Him, I fell at His feet like a dead man. But He placed His right hand on me and said, [J]“Do not be afraid. I am the First and the Last,[/J] (1:17).
[J]the Living One. I was dead, and behold, now I am alive forever and ever! And I hold the keys of Death and of Hades.[/J] (1:18).
[J]Therefore write down the things you have seen, the things that are, and the things that will happen after this.[/J] (1:19).

[J]This is the mystery of the seven stars you saw in My right hand and of the seven golden lampstands: The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands are the seven churches.[/J] (1:20).
crossRefs: Daniel 7:13: One like a son of man.
Zechariah 4:2: Lampstands and lamps before God.
Matthew 24:30: The Son of Man coming on the clouds.

translationNotes.original: Greek: Πάτμος (Patmos)
translationNotes.note: A bare rocky island in the Aegean, about thirteen square miles, roughly thirty-five miles off the coast of Asia Minor southwest of Miletus. Rome used small Aegean islands as places of banishment for offenders it did not execute; Tacitus lists men relegated to Gyaros, Amorgos and Donusa (Annals 3.68; 4.30). John says only that he was there on account of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus (1:9).

translationNotes.term: The seven cities in road order
translationNotes.original: Greek: Ἀσία (Asia, the Roman province)
translationNotes.note: Asia here is not the continent but the Roman province covering the western third of Asia Minor, in what is now Turkey. The seven cities in 1:11 are listed in the order a courier would ride them: from the port of Ephesus about forty miles north to Smyrna, forty more to Pergamum, then inland southeast to Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia and Laodicea, and back down the valley toward Ephesus. It is a postal circuit, and one messenger with one scroll could work it in that sequence.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἡ κυριακὴ ἡμέρα (he kyriake hemera)
translationNotes.note: The adjective kyriakos means belonging to the Lord, and it appears only twice in the New Testament: here, and at 1 Corinthians 11:20 of the Lord's supper. The text does not say which day of the week is meant. That is the whole of what the phrase itself tells you.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מְנוֹרָה (menorah) - Greek: λυχνία (lychnia)
translationNotes.note: A lampstand held clay or bronze oil lamps; the tabernacle and temple had a seven-branched one that burned continually before the LORD (Exodus 25:31-40; Zechariah 4:2). Here there are seven separate stands, and 1:20 says they are the seven churches. A lamp gives light only while someone keeps it filled.

translationNotes.original: Greek: τὸ Ἄλφα καὶ τὸ Ὦ (to Alpha kai to O)
translationNotes.note: The first and last letters of the Greek alphabet, the way an English speaker would say A to Z. The title is repeated at 21:6 and 22:13, and 1:17 pairs it with 'the first and the last'. Isaiah 44:6 has the LORD say the same thing in Hebrew terms: I am the first and I am the last.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ᾅδης (hades) - Hebrew: שְׁאוֹל (Sheol)
translationNotes.note: The Greek word the Septuagint uses to translate Hebrew Sheol, the realm of the dead in general rather than a place of punishment specifically. Revelation 1:18 has Christ holding the keys of Death and Hades. It is a different word from Gehenna, which comes from the Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem.

stories.keyTakeaway: John receives a vision of the glorified Christ among seven lampstands, commissioning him to write to the churches.

stories.title: 🌿 Revelation 2
summaryBullets: [J]“To the angel of the church in Ephesus write: These are the words of Him who holds the seven stars in His right hand and walks among the seven golden lampstands.[/J] (2:1).

[J]I know your deeds, your labor, and your perseverance. I know that you cannot tolerate those who are evil, and you have tested and exposed as liars those who falsely claim to be apostles.[/J] (2:2).
[J]Without growing weary, you have persevered and endured many things for the sake of My name.[/J] (2:3).
[J]But I have this against you: You have abandoned your first love.[/J] (2:4).
[J]Therefore, keep in mind how far you have fallen. Repent and perform the deeds you did at first. But if you do not repent, I will come to you and remove your lampstand from its place.[/J] (2:5).
[J]But you have this to your credit: You hate the works of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.[/J] (2:6).
[J]He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To the one who overcomes, I will grant the right to eat from the tree of life in the Paradise of God.[/J] (2:7).
[J]To the angel of the church in Smyrna write: These are the words of the First and the Last, who died and returned to life.[/J] (2:8).
[J]I know your affliction and your poverty — though you are rich! And I am aware of the slander of those who falsely claim to be Jews, but are in fact a synagogue of Satan.[/J] (2:9).

[J]Do not fear what you are about to suffer. Behold, the devil is about to throw some of you into prison to test you, and you will suffer tribulation for ten days. Be faithful even unto death, and I will give you the crown of life.[/J] (2:10).
[J]He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. The one who overcomes will not be harmed by the second death.[/J] (2:11).
[J]To the angel of the church in Pergamum write: These are the words of the One who holds the sharp, double-edged sword.[/J] (2:12).

[J]I know where you live, where the throne of Satan sits, yet you hold fast to My name. You did not deny your faith in Me, even in the days of My faithful witness Antipas, who was killed among you where Satan dwells.[/J] (2:13).

[J]But I have a few things against you, because some of you hold to the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to place a stumbling block before the Israelites so they would eat food sacrificed to idols and commit sexual immorality.[/J] (2:14).
[J]In the same way, some of you also hold to the teaching of the Nicolaitans.[/J] (2:15).
[J]Therefore repent! Otherwise I will come to you shortly and wage war against them with the sword of My mouth.[/J] (2:16).

[J]He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To the one who overcomes, I will give the hidden manna. I will also give him a white stone inscribed with a new name, known only to the one who receives it.[/J] (2:17).
[J]To the angel of the church in Thyatira write: These are the words of the Son of God, whose eyes are like a blazing fire and whose feet are like polished bronze.[/J] (2:18).
[J]I know your deeds — your love, your faith, your service, your perseverance — and your latest deeds are greater than your first.[/J] (2:19).

[J]But I have this against you: You tolerate that woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess. By her teaching she misleads My servants to be sexually immoral and to eat food sacrificed to idols.[/J] (2:20).
[J]Even though I have given her time to repent of her immorality, she is unwilling.[/J] (2:21).
[J]Behold, I will cast her onto a bed of sickness, and those who commit adultery with her will suffer great tribulation unless they repent of her deeds.[/J] (2:22).
[J]Then I will strike her children dead, and all the churches will know that I am the One who searches minds and hearts, and I will repay each of you according to your deeds.[/J] (2:23).
[J]But I say to the rest of you in Thyatira, who do not hold to her teaching and have not learned the so-called deep things of Satan: I will place no further burden upon you[/J] (2:24).
[J]than to hold fast to what you have until I come.[/J] (2:25).
[J]And to the one who overcomes and continues in My work until the end, I will give authority over the nations.[/J] (2:26).
[J]He will rule them with an iron scepter and shatter them like pottery — just as I have received authority from My Father.[/J] (2:27).
[J]And I will give him the morning star.[/J] (2:28).
[J]He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.[/J] (2:29).
crossRefs: Acts 19:23-41: The silversmiths of Ephesus riot for two hours over the trade in silver shrines of Artemis.
Genesis 2:8-9: The tree of life stands in the middle of the garden that God planted in Eden.
Numbers 25:1-3: Israel eats the sacrifices of the Moabite gods at Peor and joins itself to Baal of Peor.
1 Kings 16:29-33: Ahab marries Jezebel of Sidon, serves Baal, and sets up an altar and an Asherah pole in Samaria.
Isaiah 62:2: You shall be called by a new name that the mouth of the LORD will give.

translationNotes.original: Greek: Ἔφεσος (Ephesos)
translationNotes.note: The chief port and largest city of the province, and the home of the temple of Artemis, one of the seven wonders of the ancient world. Pliny the Elder gives it as 425 feet long by 225 wide with 127 columns sixty feet high (Natural History 36). The city ran on that temple: pilgrims, banking, asylum rights and the silversmiths' trade in miniature shrines that started the riot in Acts 19.

translationNotes.original: Greek: Σμύρνα (Smyrna)
translationNotes.note: A harbour city about forty miles north of Ephesus, now Izmir. The old city was destroyed and lay in ruins for centuries before being refounded, which is worth knowing when 2:8 addresses it as the words of the one who died and came to life. Greek writers praised the ring of public buildings crowning the hill above it as the city's crown; 2:10 promises the crown of life to the church that is about to be jailed.

translationNotes.original: Greek: Πέργαμος (Pergamos)
translationNotes.note: The old royal capital, built on a steep acropolis. On it stood the great altar of Zeus, a colonnaded platform more than a hundred feet across with a frieze of gods fighting giants, excavated by Carl Humann from 1878 and now reassembled in Berlin. The city also held the healing shrine of Asklepios, whose emblem was a serpent, and it built the first temple in Asia to Rome and Augustus in 29 BC. Verse 13 says Satan's throne is there and names Antipas, killed in the city.

translationNotes.original: Greek: Θυάτειρα (Thyateira)
translationNotes.note: An inland manufacturing town on the road southeast from Pergamum. More trade guilds are attested by inscription at Thyatira than at any other city of the province: wool workers, linen workers, dyers, tanners, potters, bakers, bronze smiths. Lydia, the dealer in purple cloth Paul meets at Philippi, came from here (Acts 16:14). In a guild town, eating and trading were social obligations, which is the setting of the charge in 2:20.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ψῆφος λευκή (psephos leuke)
translationNotes.note: A psephos is a small pebble, and it had two everyday uses: jurors dropped one in an urn to vote, white to acquit and black to condemn, and Paul uses the word that way in Acts 26:10. Pebbles or tokens were also handed out as tickets of admission to a feast or the games. The promise in 2:17 gives the stone with a new name written on it that only the one who receives it knows.

translationNotes.original: Greek: τὸ μάννα τὸ κεκρυμμένον (to manna to kekrymmenon)
translationNotes.note: A jar of manna was kept in front of the ark of the testimony as a permanent memorial of the wilderness feeding (Exodus 16:32-34; Hebrews 9:4). Manna is the food that came with no work, no market and no supplier. Verse 17 promises it to the one who overcomes in a city where the practical question was whether you could still eat if you refused the guild table.

translationNotes.original: Greek: Βαλαάμ (Balaam) - Ἰεζάβελ (Iezabel)
translationNotes.note: Two names used as precedents, and both are explained in the Old Testament. Balaam could not curse Israel, so he advised Moab how to bring Israel down instead, by sacrificial meals and sexual immorality at Peor (Numbers 25:1-3; 31:16). Jezebel was the Sidonian queen who imported Baal worship into Israel and killed the LORD's prophets (1 Kings 16:31-33; 18:4). The letters use the names for what those two did, not as identifications of who these people were.

translationNotes.original: Greek: συναγωγὴ τοῦ Σατανᾶ (synagoge tou Satana)
translationNotes.note: Phrase used in 2:9 and 3:9 for groups opposing believers and slandering them. Synagoge is the ordinary Greek word for an assembly or a gathering, and Satanas is a Hebrew loanword meaning the accuser. Both letters that use the phrase are addressed to churches under legal pressure from an accusation.

translationNotes.original: Greek: παράδεισος (paradeisos), from Persian for a walled garden
translationNotes.note: A loanword from Persian, originally a royal walled park, the same word behind the king's forest in Nehemiah 2:8. The Septuagint uses it for the garden of Eden. Jesus tells the thief on the cross 'today you will be with Me in Paradise' (Luke 23:43), and 2:7 promises the tree of life in the paradise of God.

stories.keyTakeaway: Christ addresses four churches with commendations and warnings: Ephesus has abandoned its first love despite rejecting false apostles; Smyrna faces persecution but is spiritually rich; Pergamum remains faithful despite Satan's throne there but tolerates false teachings; Thyatira practices love and service but permits the prophetess Jezebel to lead believers into sexual immorality and idolatry. Each church is promised rewards for overcoming if they repent and endure.

stories.title: 🌿 Revelation 3
summaryBullets: [J]“To the angel of the church in Sardis write: These are the words of the One who holds the seven spirits of God and the seven stars. I know your deeds; you have a reputation for being alive, yet you are dead.[/J] (3:1).
[J]Wake up and strengthen what remains, which is about to die; for I have found your deeds incomplete in the sight of My God.[/J] (3:2).
[J]Remember, then, what you have received and heard. Keep it and repent. If you do not wake up, I will come like a thief, and you will not know the hour when I will come upon you.[/J] (3:3).
[J]But you do have a few people in Sardis who have not soiled their garments, and because they are worthy, they will walk with Me in white.[/J] (3:4).
[J]Like them, he who overcomes will be dressed in white. And I will never blot out his name from the Book of Life, but I will confess his name before My Father and His angels.[/J] (3:5).
[J]He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.[/J] (3:6).

[J]To the angel of the church in Philadelphia write: These are the words of the One who is holy and true, who holds the key of David. What He opens no one can shut, and what He shuts no one can open.[/J] (3:7).

[J]I know your deeds. Behold, I have placed before you an open door, which no one can shut. I know that you have only a little strength, yet you have kept My word and have not denied My name.[/J] (3:8).
[J]As for those who belong to the synagogue of Satan, who claim to be Jews but are liars instead, I will make them come and bow down at your feet, and they will know that I love you.[/J] (3:9).
[J]Because you have kept My command to persevere, I will also keep you from the hour of testing that is about to come upon the whole world, to test those who dwell on the earth.[/J] (3:10).
[J]I am coming soon. Hold fast to what you have, so that no one will take your crown.[/J] (3:11).

[J]The one who overcomes I will make a pillar in the temple of My God, and he will never again leave it. Upon him I will write the name of My God, and the name of the city of My God (the new Jerusalem that comes down out of heaven from My God), and My new name.[/J] (3:12).
[J]He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.[/J] (3:13).
[J]To the angel of the church in Laodicea write: These are the words of the Amen, the faithful and true Witness, the Originator of God’s creation.[/J] (3:14).
[J]I know your deeds; you are neither cold nor hot. How I wish you were one or the other![/J] (3:15).
[J]So because you are lukewarm — neither hot nor cold — I am about to vomit you out of My mouth![/J] (3:16).
[J]You say, ‘I am rich; I have grown wealthy and need nothing.’ But you do not realize that you are wretched, pitiful, poor, blind, and naked.[/J] (3:17).

[J]I counsel you to buy from Me gold refined by fire so that you may become rich, white garments so that you may be clothed and your shameful nakedness not exposed, and salve to anoint your eyes so that you may see.[/J] (3:18).
[J]Those I love I rebuke and discipline. Therefore be earnest and repent.[/J] (3:19).
[J]Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will come in and dine with him, and he with Me.[/J] (3:20).
[J]To the one who overcomes, I will grant the right to sit with Me on My throne, just as I overcame and sat down with My Father on His throne.[/J] (3:21).
[J]He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.”[/J] (3:22).
crossRefs: Isaiah 22:20-23: Eliakim is given the key of the house of David on his shoulder; he opens and none shall shut.
Exodus 32:32-33: Blot me out of the book You have written, and the LORD answers that He blots out whoever has sinned against Him.
Matthew 24:42-44: Keep watch, because the thief comes at an hour you do not expect.
1 Kings 7:15-22: The two bronze pillars of the temple porch, each named, standing eighteen cubits high.
Proverbs 3:11-12: Do not despise the LORD's discipline, for the LORD reproves the one He loves.

translationNotes.original: Greek: Σάρδεις (Sardeis)
translationNotes.note: The old capital of Lydia and of Croesus, set on a spur of Mount Tmolus so steep the garrison thought one side needed no watch. It was taken that way twice. Cyrus captured it about 546 BC after a soldier watched a Lydian climb down the cliff for a dropped helmet and led a party up the same route (Herodotus 1.84), and Antiochus III took it the same way in 214 BC. Verse 3 tells the church that if it does not wake, He will come like a thief and it will not know what hour.

translationNotes.original: Greek: Φιλαδέλφεια (Philadelpheia, brotherly love)
translationNotes.note: Founded by Attalus II Philadelphus and named for his loyalty to his brother. It sat on a fault line: the earthquake of AD 17 flattened twelve cities of the province in one night (Tacitus, Annals 2.47), and Strabo writes that its walls were constantly cracking and much of the population lived outside in the fields. Verse 12 promises the one who conquers that he will be made a pillar in the temple of God and will never go out.

translationNotes.original: Greek: χλιαρός (chliaros, lukewarm)
translationNotes.note: Laodicea had no spring of its own. Water was piped in by aqueduct from springs about five miles off, and the stone pipe blocks recovered on the site are thick with mineral scale from it. Hierapolis, whose hot mineral springs are visible across the valley about six miles north, and Colossae with its cold water ten miles east, both had what Laodicea did not. The word in 3:16 for what will be done with the lukewarm mouthful is emeo, to vomit.

translationNotes.term: Gold, white garments and eye salve
translationNotes.original: Greek: κολλούριον (kollourion, eye salve)
translationNotes.note: The letter offers the city three things it was famous for producing. Laodicea was a banking centre so rich that after the earthquake of about AD 60 it rebuilt itself and refused imperial help (Tacitus, Annals 14.27). Its district was known for glossy black wool. It lay in Phrygia, the source of the powder used in ancient eye ointments, and had a medical school. Verse 18 tells it to buy gold, white clothes and eye salve from Christ instead.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἡ κλεὶς Δαυίδ (he kleis Dauid)
translationNotes.note: Verse 7 takes the wording from Isaiah 22:22, where the LORD strips the palace steward Shebna of his office and gives the key of the house of David to Eliakim, who opens and none shuts. A royal steward's key was a physical badge of office, carried on the shoulder, controlling access to the king. The image is authority over admission.

translationNotes.original: Greek: στῦλος (stylos, pillar)
translationNotes.note: Solomon's temple had two free-standing bronze pillars at its porch, each with a name of its own, Jachin and Boaz (1 Kings 7:15-22). Greek temples carried the names of benefactors and priests carved on their columns. In an earthquake city, a pillar that never goes out is a promise with weight.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἡ βίβλος τῆς ζωῆς (he biblos tes zoes)
translationNotes.note: Cities kept a citizen register, and a name struck off it ended a man's legal standing. The image is older than that: Moses asks to be blotted out of the book God has written (Exodus 32:32-33), and the psalmist speaks of the book of the living (Psalm 69:28). Verse 5 promises the opposite, that the name will not be erased and will be acknowledged before the Father.

stories.keyTakeaway: Christ addresses three churches: Sardis is spiritually dead despite its reputation and must repent or face sudden judgment, though a few remain faithful; Philadelphia is weak but obedient and will be protected from coming trials; Laodicea is lukewarm and self-deceived about its poverty, and Christ calls it to buy spiritual refinement and repent.

stories.title: 🕊️ Revelation 4
summaryBullets: After this I looked and saw a door standing open in heaven. And the voice I had previously heard speak to me like a trumpet was saying, [J]“Come up here, and I will show you what must happen after these things.”[/J] (4:1).
At once I was in the Spirit, and I saw a throne standing in heaven, with someone seated on it. (4:2).
The One seated there looked like jasper and carnelian, and a rainbow that gleamed like an emerald encircled the throne. (4:3).
Surrounding the throne were twenty-four other thrones, and on these thrones sat twenty-four elders dressed in white, with golden crowns on their heads. (4:4).
From the throne came flashes of lightning, rumblings, and peals of thunder. Before the throne burned seven torches of fire. These are the seven spirits of God. (4:5).
And before the throne was something like a sea of glass, as clear as crystal. In the center, around the throne, were four living creatures, covered with eyes in front and back. (4:6).
The first living creature was like a lion, the second like a calf, the third had a face like a man, and the fourth was like an eagle in flight. (4:7).

And each of the four living creatures had six wings and was covered with eyes all around and within. Day and night they never stop saying: “Holy, Holy, Holy, is the Lord God Almighty, who was and is and is to come!” (4:8).
And whenever the living creatures give glory, honor, and thanks to the One seated on the throne, who lives forever and ever, (4:9).
the twenty-four elders fall down before the One seated on the throne, and they worship Him who lives forever and ever. They cast their crowns before the throne, saying: (4:10).
“Worthy are You, our Lord and God, to receive glory and honor and power, for You created all things; by Your will they exist and were created.” (4:11).
crossRefs: Isaiah 6:2-3: Vision of seraphim crying 'Holy, holy, holy.'
Ezekiel 1:5-10: Vision of four living creatures.
Colossians 1:16: All things created through him.

translationNotes.original: Greek: τὰ ἑπτὰ πνεύματα τοῦ θεοῦ (ta hepta pneumata tou theou)
translationNotes.note: Symbolic for the fullness of the Holy Spirit.

translationNotes.original: Greek: θάλασσα ὑαλίνη (thalassa hualinē)
translationNotes.note: Vivid image of a vast expanse before the throne, like crystal.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ζῷα (zōa)
translationNotes.note: Heavenly beings with attributes of lion, ox, man, eagle; echo Ezekiel’s vision.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ (qāḏôš qāḏôš qāḏôš), Greek: ἅγιος ἅγιος ἅγιος (hágios hágios hágios, NT), Aramaic: קדיש קדיש קדיש (qaddiš qaddiš qaddiš)
translationNotes.note: Threefold repetition is a superlative expression of God’s absolute holiness.

translationNotes.original: Greek: προσκυνέω (proskyneo)
translationNotes.note: To fall down in homage, 'kiss toward.' Used when the Magi worshiped Jesus (Matthew 2:11), when Jesus taught about worship in spirit and truth (John 4:23-24), when the healed blind man bowed before him (John 9:38), and in Revelation where heavenly beings fall in worship (Revelation 4:10; 19:10).

stories.keyTakeaway: John is taken into heaven’s throne room where he sees God’s glory, the elders, the living creatures, and their ceaseless worship.

stories.title: 📜 Revelation 5
summaryBullets: Then I saw a scroll in the right hand of the One seated on the throne. It had writing on both sides and was sealed with seven seals. (5:1).
And I saw a mighty angel proclaiming in a loud voice, “Who is worthy to break the seals and open the scroll?” (5:2).
But no one in heaven or on earth or under the earth was able to open the scroll or look inside it. (5:3).
And I began to weep bitterly, because no one was found worthy to open the scroll or look inside it. (5:4).
Then one of the elders said to me, “Do not weep! Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has triumphed to open the scroll and its seven seals.” (5:5).

Then I saw a Lamb who appeared to have been slain, standing in the center of the throne, encircled by the four living creatures and the elders. The Lamb had seven horns and seven eyes, which represent the seven spirits of God sent out into all the earth. (5:6).
And He came and took the scroll from the right hand of the One seated on the throne. (5:7).

When He had taken the scroll, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb. Each one had a harp, and they were holding golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints. (5:8).

And they sang a new song: “Worthy are You to take the scroll and open its seals, because You were slain, and by Your blood You purchased for God those from every tribe and tongue and people and nation. (5:9).
You have made them to be a kingdom and priests to serve our God, and they will reign upon the earth.” (5:10).
Then I looked, and I heard the voices of many angels encircling the throne, and the living creatures and the elders. And their number was myriads of myriads and thousands of thousands. (5:11).
In a loud voice they were saying: “Worthy is the Lamb who was slain, to receive power and riches and wisdom and strength and honor and glory and blessing!” (5:12).

And I heard every creature in heaven and on earth and under the earth and in the sea, and all that is in them, saying: “To Him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb be praise and honor and glory and power forever and ever!” (5:13).
And the four living creatures said, “Amen,” and the elders fell down and worshiped. (5:14).
crossRefs: Genesis 49:9-10: Lion of Judah.
Isaiah 53:7: Lamb led to the slaughter.
John 1:29: Behold, the Lamb of God.

translationNotes.term: A scroll sealed with seven seals
translationNotes.original: Greek: βιβλίον κατεσφραγισμένον σφραγῖσιν ἑπτά (biblion katesphragismenon sphragisin hepta)
translationNotes.note: This is a legal instrument, not a book. Roman law required a sealed will to carry the seals of seven witnesses, and important deeds were written twice: the full text inside, rolled and sealed, and a summary on the outside that anyone could read. Jeremiah 32:10-14 shows the same practice, a sealed deed of purchase with an open copy stored beside it. Verse 1 describes exactly that document, written within and on the back, and the question in 5:2 is not who can read it but who has the standing to break the seals.

translationNotes.term: Lion of Judah, Root of David
translationNotes.original: Greek: ὁ λέων ὁ ἐκ τῆς φυλῆς Ἰούδα (ho leon ho ek tes phyles Iouda)
translationNotes.note: Both titles are quotations. Jacob calls Judah a lion's cub and says the sceptre will not depart from him (Genesis 49:9-10), and Isaiah speaks of a shoot from the stump of Jesse and a root that will stand as a signal to the peoples (Isaiah 11:1, 10). The elder announces a lion; what John turns and sees is a lamb.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἀρνίον (arnion, little lamb)
translationNotes.note: The word is a diminutive, a lamb rather than a ram, and Revelation uses it about the Lamb twenty-eight times. Verse 6 says it stands as though slain, that is, bearing the wound. Behind it sit the Passover lamb of Exodus 12, the lamb led to the slaughter of Isaiah 53:7, and John the Baptist's words in John 1:29.

translationNotes.original: Greek: κέρατα ἑπτὰ καὶ ὀφθαλμοὺς ἑπτά (kerata hepta kai ophthalmous hepta)
translationNotes.note: A horn is the standard image for strength in Scripture, taken from what an ox or ram does with them (Deuteronomy 33:17; 1 Samuel 2:10; Psalm 75:10). The seven eyes are explained in the verse itself as the seven spirits of God sent out into all the earth, wording drawn from Zechariah 4:10, where the seven eyes of the LORD range through the whole earth.

translationNotes.original: Greek: φιάλας χρυσᾶς γεμούσας θυμιαμάτων (phialas chrysas gemousas thymiamaton)
translationNotes.note: The text says outright what they are: the prayers of the saints (5:8). Incense burned on the golden altar morning and evening while the people prayed outside (Exodus 30:1-8; Luke 1:8-10), and Psalm 141:2 asks that prayer be counted as incense. The same shallow gold bowls turn up again in chapter 16 holding something else entirely.

translationNotes.original: Greek: βασιλείαν καὶ ἱερεῖς (basileian kai hiereis)
translationNotes.note: The song in 5:9-10 quotes Exodus 19:6, where God tells Israel at Sinai that they will be to Him a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. The line 'from every tribe and tongue and people and nation' is the addition. 1 Peter 2:9 applies the same Sinai wording.

stories.keyTakeaway: Only the slain yet risen Lamb is worthy to open the scroll, and all creation worships him with God.

stories.title: 🌿 Revelation 6
summaryBullets: Then I watched as the Lamb opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures say in a voice like thunder, “Come!” (6:1).
So I looked and saw a white horse, and its rider held a bow. And he was given a crown, and he rode out to overcome and conquer. (6:2).
And when the Lamb opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature say, “Come!” (6:3).
Then another horse went forth. It was bright red, and its rider was granted permission to take away peace from the earth and to make men slay one another. And he was given a great sword. (6:4).
And when the Lamb opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature say, “Come!” Then I looked and saw a black horse, and its rider held in his hand a pair of scales. (6:5).

And I heard what sounded like a voice from among the four living creatures, saying, “A quart of wheat for a denarius, and three quarts of barley for a denarius, and do not harm the oil and wine.” (6:6).
And when the Lamb opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature say, “Come!” (6:7).

Then I looked and saw a pale green horse. Its rider’s name was Death, and Hades followed close behind. And they were given authority over a fourth of the earth, to kill by sword, by famine, by plague, and by the beasts of the earth. (6:8).
And when the Lamb opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of those who had been slain for the word of God and for the testimony they had upheld. (6:9).
And they cried out in a loud voice, “How long, O Lord, holy and true, until You judge those who dwell upon the earth and avenge our blood?” (6:10).
Then each of them was given a white robe and told to rest a little while longer until the full number of their fellow servants, their brothers, were killed, just as they had been killed. (6:11).
And I watched as the Lamb opened the sixth seal, and there was a great earthquake, and the sun became black like sackcloth of goat hair, and the whole moon turned blood red, (6:12).
and the stars of the sky fell to the earth like unripe figs dropping from a tree shaken by a great wind. (6:13).
The sky receded like a scroll being rolled up, and every mountain and island was moved from its place. (6:14).
Then the kings of the earth, the nobles, the commanders, the rich, the mighty, and every slave and free man hid in the caves and among the rocks of the mountains. (6:15).
And they said to the mountains and the rocks, “Fall on us and hide us from the face of the One seated on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb. (6:16).
For the great day of Their wrath has come, and who is able to withstand it?” (6:17).
crossRefs: Zechariah 6:1-8: Vision of four horsemen.
Matthew 24:7: Wars, famines, earthquakes.
Joel 2:31: Sun darkened, moon to blood.

translationNotes.term: A quart of wheat for a denarius
translationNotes.original: Greek: χοῖνιξ σίτου δηναρίου (choinix sitou denariou)
translationNotes.note: A choinix is about a quart, and it was reckoned as one man's grain ration for one day; Herodotus (7.187) uses exactly that figure to calculate the supply of Xerxes' army. So the cry in 6:6 prices a single day's bread for a single man at a full day's wage, with nothing left for a family or for anything else. In ordinary times a denarius bought something like eight to sixteen quarts of wheat. This is famine pricing, roughly ten times normal, announced as a market rate.

translationNotes.original: Latin: denarius - Greek: δηνάριον (denarion)
translationNotes.note: A Roman silver coin, the standard day's wage for a labourer, which is the going rate Jesus names in the parable of the vineyard (Matthew 20:2). It carried the emperor's head, which is why it was the coin produced in the tax question (Mark 12:16). Two denarii covered the injured man's care at the inn (Luke 10:35).

translationNotes.original: Greek: ζυγός (zygos, balance or yoke)
translationNotes.note: Grain was normally sold by the sack and eaten without counting. Weighing it out on a balance is itself a sign of scarcity, and the Law uses that image for judgment: they shall deliver your bread again by weight, and you shall eat and not be satisfied (Leviticus 26:26; Ezekiel 4:16). The rider holds the balance, and the price is called out from the middle of the living creatures.

translationNotes.term: Do not harm the oil and the wine
translationNotes.original: Greek: τὸ ἔλαιον καὶ τὸν οἶνον μὴ ἀδικήσῃς (to elaion kai ton oinon me adikeses)
translationNotes.note: Olives and vines are deep-rooted perennials that survive a dry year which destroys a grain crop, and both were the region's cash exports rather than its daily food. The limit set in 6:6 spares the two things a poor man cannot eat and leaves the grain ruined. Grain, oil and wine are the standard triad for a land's produce (Deuteronomy 7:13; Joel 2:19).

translationNotes.original: Greek: χλωρός (chloros)
translationNotes.note: Chloros is the ordinary word for the green of growing things; Mark 6:39 uses it of green grass, and it is the root of English chlorophyll. Applied to a face or a body it means the greenish grey of sickness and death. The colour is the point of the rider's name.

translationNotes.term: Sword, famine, pestilence and wild beasts
translationNotes.original: Greek: ῥομφαίᾳ καὶ ἐν λιμῷ καὶ ἐν θανάτῳ καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν θηρίων (rhomphaia, limos, thanatos, theria)
translationNotes.note: The four instruments listed in 6:8 are the same four the LORD names in Ezekiel 14:21 as His four disastrous acts of judgment against Jerusalem: sword, famine, wild beasts and pestilence. The word rendered pestilence here is thanatos, death, which is how the Septuagint often translates the Hebrew for plague. The list is a quotation, not a new inventory.

translationNotes.original: Greek: σάκκος τρίχινος (sakkos trichinos, sackcloth of hair)
translationNotes.note: Sackcloth was woven from black goat hair, coarse and dark, and worn against the skin as a sign of mourning. Verse 12 does not just say the sun went dark; it says it went the colour of mourning cloth, and the moon the colour of blood. Joel 2:31 and Acts 2:20 use the same pair of images.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ᾅδης (hades) - Hebrew: שְׁאוֹל (Sheol)
translationNotes.note: Hades is not hell. It is the term the Septuagint uses to render Hebrew Sheol, the common realm of the dead. In 6:8 Hades follows the fourth rider as a named figure, the way a burial detail follows an army. It is distinct from Gehenna and from the lake of fire, into which 20:14 says Death and Hades are themselves thrown.

stories.keyTakeaway: Opening of six seals reveals horsemen bringing conquest, war, famine, death, martyrs seeking justice, and cosmic upheaval before judgment.

headings.text: The First Seal: The White Horse

stories.title: 📜 Revelation 7
summaryBullets: After this I saw four angels standing at the four corners of the earth, holding back its four winds so that no wind would blow on land or sea or on any tree. (7:1).
And I saw another angel ascending from the east, with the seal of the living God. And he called out in a loud voice to the four angels who had been given power to harm the land and the sea: (7:2).
“Do not harm the land or sea or trees until we have placed a seal on the foreheads of the servants of our God.” (7:3).
And I heard the number of those who were sealed, 144,000 from all the tribes of Israel: (7:4).
From the tribe of Judah 12,000 were sealed, from the tribe of Reuben 12,000, from the tribe of Gad 12,000, (7:5).
from the tribe of Asher 12,000, from the tribe of Naphtali 12,000, from the tribe of Manasseh 12,000, (7:6).
from the tribe of Simeon 12,000, from the tribe of Levi 12,000, from the tribe of Issachar 12,000, (7:7).
from the tribe of Zebulun 12,000, from the tribe of Joseph 12,000, and from the tribe of Benjamin 12,000. (7:8).

After this I looked and saw a multitude too large to count, from every nation and tribe and people and tongue, standing before the throne and before the Lamb. They were wearing white robes and holding palm branches in their hands. (7:9).
And they cried out in a loud voice: “Salvation to our God, who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!” (7:10).
And all the angels stood around the throne and around the elders and the four living creatures. And they fell facedown before the throne and worshiped God, (7:11).
saying, “Amen! Blessing and glory and wisdom and thanks and honor and power and strength be to our God forever and ever! Amen.” (7:12).
Then one of the elders addressed me: “These in white robes,” he asked, “who are they, and where have they come from?” (7:13).
“Sir,” I answered, “you know.” So he replied, “These are the ones who have come out of the great tribulation; they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb. (7:14).
For this reason, they are before the throne of God and serve Him day and night in His temple; and the One seated on the throne will spread His tabernacle over them. (7:15).
‘Never again will they hunger, and never will they thirst; nor will the sun beat down upon them, nor any scorching heat.’ (7:16).
For the Lamb in the center of the throne will be their shepherd. ‘He will lead them to springs of living water,’ and ‘God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.’” (7:17).
crossRefs: Ezekiel 9:4: Marking the servants of God.
John 10:11: The good shepherd.
Isaiah 25:8: God wipes away tears.

translationNotes.original: Greek: σφραγίς (sphragis, seal)
translationNotes.note: A seal marked ownership. Documents were sealed with a signet, cattle were branded, slaves and soldiers carried marks, and a sealed jar or door was one nobody had opened. Ezekiel 9:4 is the passage behind this scene: a man with a writing case goes through Jerusalem putting a mark on the foreheads of those who grieve over what is done in the city, and the killing passes them by. The counterfeit of it appears in 13:16.

translationNotes.original: Greek: τέσσαρες γωνίαι τῆς γῆς (tessares goniai tes ges)
translationNotes.note: Naming the four corners and the four winds is the ordinary ancient way of saying every direction of the compass, exactly as English says the four corners of the earth. Scripture uses it for the scattering and the gathering of peoples (Jeremiah 49:36; Ezekiel 37:9; Daniel 7:2; Matthew 24:31). It is a bearing, not a shape.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἑκατὸν τεσσεράκοντα τέσσαρες χιλιάδες (hekaton tesserakonta tessares chiliades)
translationNotes.note: Twelve thousand from each of twelve tribes, listed tribe by tribe in 7:5-8. Immediately afterward John says he looked and saw a great multitude that no one could number, from every nation, tribe, people and tongue (7:9). The chapter gives a counted group and an uncountable one, in that order.

translationNotes.original: Greek: φοίνικες (phoinikes, palm branches)
translationNotes.note: Palm branches were carried at the Feast of Booths, where Leviticus 23:40 commands branches of palm and leafy trees and willows, and they were waved at victory processions; the crowd used them when Jesus entered Jerusalem (John 12:13). Booths was the feast of shelters, and 7:15 says the one on the throne will shelter them with His presence, using the verb for pitching a tent over someone.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἡ θλῖψις ἡ μεγάλη (he thlipsis he megale)
translationNotes.note: Thlipsis means pressure or crushing, the word for a weight bearing down; it is used of ordinary persecution throughout the New Testament (John 16:33; Acts 14:22). Here it carries the article and the adjective, the great pressure, and 7:14 says these are the ones coming out of it. Jesus uses the same phrase in Matthew 24:21.

translationNotes.term: He will shepherd them and lead them to springs
translationNotes.original: Greek: ποιμανεῖ αὐτοὺς καὶ ὁδηγήσει αὐτοὺς ἐπὶ ζωῆς πηγὰς ὑδάτων (poimanei autous kai hodegesei autous epi zoes pegas hydaton)
translationNotes.note: Verses 16-17 are stitched from two Old Testament passages. Isaiah 49:10 says they shall not hunger or thirst, neither shall the heat or sun strike them, for He who has pity on them will lead them by springs of water. Isaiah 25:8 says He will wipe away tears from all faces. The Lamb is put in the shepherd's place.

stories.keyTakeaway: God seals his servants for protection, shows the redeemed multitude from all nations worshiping, and promises eternal shelter, provision, and comfort through the Lamb.

stories.title: 🌿 Revelation 8
summaryBullets: When the Lamb opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour. (8:1).
And I saw the seven angels who stand before God, and they were given seven trumpets. (8:2).
Then another angel, who had a golden censer, came and stood at the altar. He was given much incense to offer, along with the prayers of all the saints, on the golden altar before the throne. (8:3).
And the smoke of the incense, together with the prayers of the saints, rose up before God from the hand of the angel. (8:4).
Then the angel took the censer, filled it with fire from the altar, and hurled it to the earth; and there were peals of thunder, rumblings, flashes of lightning, and an earthquake. (8:5).
And the seven angels with the seven trumpets prepared to sound them. (8:6).

Then the first angel sounded his trumpet, and hail and fire mixed with blood were hurled down upon the earth. A third of the earth was burned up, along with a third of the trees and all the green grass. (8:7).
Then the second angel sounded his trumpet, and something like a great mountain burning with fire was thrown into the sea. A third of the sea turned to blood, (8:8).
a third of the living creatures in the sea died, and a third of the ships were destroyed. (8:9).
Then the third angel sounded his trumpet, and a great star burning like a torch fell from heaven and landed on a third of the rivers and on the springs of water. (8:10).
The name of the star is Wormwood. A third of the waters turned bitter like wormwood oil, and many people died from the bitter waters. (8:11).

Then the fourth angel sounded his trumpet, and a third of the sun and moon and stars were struck. A third of the stars were darkened, a third of the day was without light, and a third of the night as well. (8:12).

And as I observed, I heard an eagle flying overhead, calling in a loud voice, “Woe! Woe! Woe to those who dwell on the earth, because of the trumpet blasts about to be sounded by the remaining three angels!” (8:13).
crossRefs: Exodus 30:1-10: The golden altar of incense, burned on every morning and evening, standing before the veil.
Luke 1:8-11: The people pray outside at the hour of incense while the priest burns it inside the sanctuary.
Psalm 141:2: Let my prayer be set before You as incense, the lifting of my hands as the evening sacrifice.
Joshua 6:12-20: Seven priests carry seven trumpets around the city for seven days, and on the seventh the wall falls.
Jeremiah 9:15: I will feed this people wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink.

translationNotes.term: Silence for about half an hour
translationNotes.original: Greek: σιγὴ ὡς ἡμιώριον (sige hos hemiorion)
translationNotes.note: The only measured stretch of silence in Scripture, and it follows six seals of noise. In the temple the moment of incense was the quiet one, with the crowd outside praying and no sound from within (Luke 1:10). Habakkuk 2:20 and Zephaniah 1:7 both call for silence before the LORD when judgment is at hand.

translationNotes.original: Greek: λιβανωτός (libanotos, censer)
translationNotes.note: A fire pan for carrying live coals from the altar and burning incense on them. The high priest carried one behind the veil on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:12-13), and the daily incense went up on the golden altar morning and evening. In 8:5 the angel fills the same censer with fire from the altar and throws it to the earth, so the vessel that carried up the prayers brings down the answer.

translationNotes.original: Greek: σάλπιγξ (salpinx) - Hebrew: חֲצֹצְרָה (chatsotserah)
translationNotes.note: Not a musical instrument but a signal. Numbers 10:1-10 gives the priests two silver trumpets for summoning the assembly, breaking camp, going to war and sounding over the offerings. Seven trumpets circled Jericho for seven days (Joshua 6). A trumpet in this book is an announcement everyone hears at once.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לַעֲנָה (la'anah) - Greek: ἄψινθος (apsinthos)
translationNotes.note: A shrub of the Artemisia family, grey-leaved and intensely bitter, common in dry country. Scripture uses it as the standard image for what is bitter and poisonous to drink: a root bearing poisonous fruit and wormwood (Deuteronomy 29:18), justice turned to wormwood (Amos 5:7), and the LORD feeding a rebellious people wormwood and poisoned water (Jeremiah 9:15). In 8:11 the star is given the name.

translationNotes.original: Greek: τὸ τρίτον (to triton, the third)
translationNotes.note: The fraction runs through the whole chapter: a third of the earth, the trees, the sea, the creatures, the ships, the rivers, the sun, the moon, the stars, the day and the night. It is a limited stroke, larger than the fourth given to the horsemen in 6:8 and short of the whole. Ezekiel 5:1-4 divides the prophet's shorn hair into thirds for three different judgments.

stories.keyTakeaway: The seventh seal opens to silence; seven angels receive trumpets and an angel offers incense with the prayers of God's people at the altar. As the first four angels sound their trumpets, devastating plagues strike the earth - hail and fire burn vegetation, a burning mountain poisons the sea, the star Wormwood contaminates water supplies, and darkness covers a third of the sky; an eagle warns of three more woes to come.

stories.title: 📜 Revelation 9
summaryBullets: Then the fifth angel sounded his trumpet, and I saw a star that had fallen from heaven to earth, and it was given the key to the pit of the Abyss. (9:1).
The star opened the pit of the Abyss, and smoke rose out of it like the smoke of a great furnace, and the sun and the air were darkened by the smoke from the pit. (9:2).
And out of the smoke, locusts descended on the earth, and they were given power like that of the scorpions of the earth. (9:3).
They were told not to harm the grass of the earth or any plant or tree, but only those who did not have the seal of God on their foreheads. (9:4).
The locusts were not given power to kill them, but only to torment them for five months, and their torment was like the stinging of a scorpion. (9:5).
In those days men will seek death and will not find it; they will long to die, but death will escape them. (9:6).
And the locusts looked like horses prepared for battle, with something like crowns of gold on their heads; and their faces were like the faces of men. (9:7).
They had hair like that of women, and teeth like those of lions. (9:8).
They also had breastplates like breastplates of iron, and the sound of their wings was like the roar of many horses and chariots rushing into battle. (9:9).
They had tails with stingers like scorpions, which had the power to injure people for five months. (9:10).
They were ruled by a king, the angel of the Abyss. His name in Hebrew is Abaddon, and in Greek it is Apollyon. (9:11).
The first woe has passed. Behold, two woes are still to follow. (9:12).
Then the sixth angel sounded his trumpet, and I heard a voice from the four horns of the golden altar before God (9:13).
saying to the sixth angel with the trumpet, “Release the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates.” (9:14).
So the four angels who had been prepared for this hour and day and month and year were released to kill a third of mankind. (9:15).
And the number of mounted troops was two hundred million; I heard their number. (9:16).

Now the horses and riders in my vision looked like this: The riders had breastplates the colors of fire, sapphire, and sulfur. The heads of the horses were like the heads of lions, and out of their mouths proceeded fire, smoke, and sulfur. (9:17).
A third of mankind was killed by the three plagues of fire, smoke, and sulfur that proceeded from their mouths. (9:18).
For the power of the horses was in their mouths and in their tails; indeed, their tails were like snakes, having heads with which to inflict harm. (9:19).

Now the rest of mankind who were not killed by these plagues still did not repent of the works of their hands. They did not stop worshiping demons and idols of gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood, which cannot see or hear or walk. (9:20).
Furthermore, they did not repent of their murder, sorcery, sexual immorality, and theft. (9:21).
crossRefs: Exodus 10:12-15: Locusts cover the whole land of Egypt until it is dark, and eat every green thing left by the hail.
Joel 1:2-7: A nation with the teeth of a lion has come up on the land and stripped the vines and the fig trees bare.
Joel 2:1-11: Their appearance is like horses, and they run like war horses, with a noise like chariots on the mountaintops.
Isaiah 14:12-15: A taunt against the king of Babylon, fallen from heaven, cut down to the ground, brought to the pit.
Psalm 115:4-8: Idols of silver and gold, the work of human hands, which cannot see or hear or walk.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἄβυσσος (abyssos, bottomless) - φρέαρ (phrear, a well or shaft)
translationNotes.note: Abyssos is the Septuagint word for the deep of Genesis 1:2 and for the depths of the sea, and in the New Testament it names the place of confinement for spirits; the demons of Luke 8:31 beg not to be sent there. What is opened in 9:1-2 is a phrear, a shaft or well, and what comes up first is smoke like a great furnace that darkens the sun.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἀκρίδες (akrides)
translationNotes.note: The desert locust is a real and recurring catastrophe in that part of the world. A swarm can cover hundreds of square miles, blot out the sun, and each insect eats roughly its own weight in vegetation every day, so a field can be stripped to bare stems in hours. Exodus 10 and Joel 1-2 describe it as it happens. What makes 9:4 strange is the reversal: these are told to harm no grass, no green thing and no tree, only people.

translationNotes.original: Greek: μῆνας πέντε (menas pente)
translationNotes.note: Repeated twice, in 9:5 and 9:10. Five months is about the span of a desert locust's adult life and of the swarming season from spring into late summer. The torment is given a fixed end and it is stated twice.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֲבַדּוֹן (Abaddon, destruction) - Greek: Ἀπολλύων (Apollyon, destroyer)
translationNotes.note: The text gives the name in both languages, which it does nowhere else. Abaddon is a real Hebrew word used in the Old Testament for the place of ruin, paired with Sheol and the grave (Job 26:6; 28:22; Proverbs 15:11). Apollyon is a Greek participle meaning the one destroying. He is called the angel of the abyss and king over the locusts.

translationNotes.term: Twice ten thousand times ten thousand
translationNotes.original: Greek: δισμυριάδες μυριάδων (dismyriades myriadon)
translationNotes.note: A myrias is ten thousand, and the phrase in 9:16 multiplies it: two hundred million if taken as arithmetic. The same construction appears in 5:11 for the angels around the throne. Greek used myrias both as a precise number and as the ordinary word for a countless crowd, which is where English gets myriad.

translationNotes.original: Greek: φαρμακεία (pharmakeia)
translationNotes.note: The word in 9:21 is the root of English pharmacy, and it covers drugs, potions and the preparation of them for magical use. It sits in a list with murders, immorality and thefts, and with the worship of idols of gold, silver, bronze, stone and wood that cannot see or hear or walk. Paul puts the same word in his list at Galatians 5:20.

stories.keyTakeaway: A fallen star opens the Abyss, releasing locusts with scorpion power to torment the unsealed for five months under their king Abaddon; then four angels at the Euphrates are released to kill a third of mankind with two hundred million mounted troops, yet survivors refuse to repent of idolatry and wickedness.

stories.title: 📜 Revelation 10
summaryBullets: Then I saw another mighty angel coming down from heaven, wrapped in a cloud, with a rainbow above his head. His face was like the sun, and his legs were like pillars of fire. (10:1).
He held in his hand a small scroll, which lay open. He placed his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land. (10:2).
Then he cried out in a loud voice like the roar of a lion. And when he cried out, the seven thunders sounded their voices. (10:3).
When the seven thunders had spoken, I was about to put it in writing. But I heard a voice from heaven saying, “Seal up what the seven thunders have said, and do not write it down.” (10:4).
Then the angel I had seen standing on the sea and on the land lifted up his right hand to heaven. (10:5).
And he swore by Him who lives forever and ever, who created heaven and everything in it, the earth and everything in it, and the sea and everything in it: “There will be no more delay! (10:6).
But in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he begins to sound his trumpet, the mystery of God will be fulfilled, just as He proclaimed to His servants the prophets.” (10:7).
Then the voice that I had heard from heaven spoke to me again, saying, “Go, take the small scroll that lies open in the hand of the angel standing on the sea and on the land.” (10:8).
And I went to the angel and said, “Give me the small scroll.” “Take it and eat it,” he said. “It will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be as sweet as honey.” (10:9).
So I took the small scroll from the angel’s hand and ate it, and it was as sweet as honey in my mouth. But when I had eaten it, my stomach turned bitter. (10:10).
And they told me, “You must prophesy again about many peoples and nations and tongues and kings.” (10:11).
crossRefs: Ezekiel 3:1-3: Eating the scroll.
Daniel 12:7: Swearing by him who lives forever.
Amos 3:7: The Lord reveals his secrets to prophets.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מְגִלָּה קְטַנָּה (megillāh qəṭannāh, sense), Greek: βιβλαρίδιον (biblarídion, NT), Aramaic: מגילתא זעירתא (megillātā zeʿīrtā)
translationNotes.note: Diminutive form of scroll; distinct from the sealed scroll of chapter 5, symbolizing a prophetic commission for John.

translationNotes.original: Greek: αἱ ἑπτὰ βρονταί (hai hepta brontai)
translationNotes.note: Unrevealed utterances; John is forbidden to record them, showing hidden aspects of God’s plan.

translationNotes.original: Greek: τὸ μυστήριον τοῦ θεοῦ (to mystērion tou theou)
translationNotes.note: God’s hidden purpose, announced to the prophets, fulfilled at the seventh trumpet.

stories.keyTakeaway: A mighty angel gives John a little scroll to eat, symbolizing prophecy both sweet and bitter, foretelling judgment and witness.

headings.text: The Angel and the Small Scroll

stories.title: 🌿 Revelation 11
summaryBullets: Then I was given a measuring rod like a staff and was told, “Go and measure the temple of God and the altar, and count the number of worshipers there. (11:1).
But exclude the courtyard outside the temple. Do not measure it, because it has been given over to the nations, and they will trample the holy city for 42 months. (11:2).
And I will empower my two witnesses, and they will prophesy for 1,260 days, clothed in sackcloth.” (11:3).
These witnesses are the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand before the Lord of the earth. (11:4).
If anyone wants to harm them, fire proceeds from their mouths and devours their enemies. In this way, anyone who wants to harm them must be killed. (11:5).

These witnesses have power to shut the sky so that no rain will fall during the days of their prophecy, and power to turn the waters into blood and to strike the earth with every kind of plague as often as they wish. (11:6).
When the two witnesses have finished their testimony, the beast that comes up from the Abyss will wage war with them, and will overpower and kill them. (11:7).
Their bodies will lie in the street of the great city — figuratively called Sodom and Egypt — where their Lord was also crucified. (11:8).
For three and a half days all peoples and tribes and tongues and nations will view their bodies and will not permit them to be laid in a tomb. (11:9).
And those who dwell on the earth will gloat over them and celebrate and send one another gifts, because these two prophets had tormented them. (11:10).
But after the three and a half days, the breath of life from God entered the two witnesses, and they stood on their feet, and great fear fell upon those who saw them. (11:11).
And the witnesses heard a loud voice from heaven saying, “Come up here.” And they went up to heaven in a cloud as their enemies watched them. (11:12).
And in that hour there was a great earthquake, and a tenth of the city collapsed. Seven thousand were killed in the quake, and the rest were terrified and gave glory to the God of heaven. (11:13).
The second woe has passed. Behold, the third woe is coming shortly. (11:14).

Then the seventh angel sounded his trumpet, and loud voices called out in heaven: “The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ, and He will reign forever and ever.” (11:15).
And the twenty-four elders who sit on their thrones before God fell on their faces and worshiped God, (11:16).
saying: “We give thanks to You, O Lord God Almighty, the One who is and who was, because You have taken Your great power and have begun to reign. (11:17).

The nations were enraged, and Your wrath has come. The time has come to judge the dead and to reward Your servants the prophets, as well as the saints and those who fear Your name, both small and great— and to destroy those who destroy the earth.” (11:18).

Then the temple of God in heaven was opened, and the ark of His covenant appeared in His temple. And there were flashes of lightning, rumblings, peals of thunder, an earthquake, and a great hailstorm. (11:19).
crossRefs: Zechariah 4:3: Two olive trees and lampstands.
Exodus 7:20: Water turned to blood.
1 Kings 17:1: Elijah stops rain.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁנַיִם חֹדֶשׁ (ʾarbaʿîm û-šənayim ḥōdeš); Greek: μῆνας τεσσεράκοντα δύο / ἡμέρας χιλίας διακοσίας ἑξήκοντα (mēnas tessarákonta dýo / hēméras chilías diakosías hexḗkonta, NT); Aramaic: ירחין ארבעין ותרין / יומין אלפא ומאתן ושיתין (yārḥīn ʾarbaʿīn ū-trēn / yōmīn ʾalpā ū-meʾatān ū-šiṯṭīn)
translationNotes.note: Symbolic prophetic period (3½ years), recurring in Daniel and Revelation to mark tribulation and witness.

translationNotes.original: Greek: θηρίον ἀναβαῖνον ἐκ τῆς ἀβύσσου (thērion anabainon ek tēs abyssou)
translationNotes.note: First mention of the beast that rises from the abyss, later described in detail in chapters 13 and 17.

translationNotes.original: Greek: κιβωτὸς τῆς διαθήκης (kibōtos tēs diathēkēs)
translationNotes.note: Sacred chest symbolizing God’s presence, now revealed in the heavenly temple.

A coarse, dark goat-hair fabric worn against bare skin as a universal sign of mourning, repentance, or distress (1 Kings 21:27; Jonah 3:5; Matthew 11:21). Wearing it publicly broadcast grief or contrition; the discomfort itself was part of the symbolism.
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שַׂק (saq); Greek: σάκκος (sakkos)

stories.keyTakeaway: John sees two witnesses prophesy, are killed, raised, and ascend; the seventh trumpet sounds, declaring Christ’s eternal reign.

stories.title: 📜 Revelation 12
summaryBullets: And a great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed in the sun, with the moon under her feet and a crown of twelve stars on her head. (12:1).
She was pregnant and crying out in the pain and agony of giving birth. (12:2).
Then another sign appeared in heaven: a huge red dragon with seven heads, ten horns, and seven royal crowns on his heads. (12:3).

His tail swept a third of the stars from the sky, hurling them to the earth. And the dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, ready to devour her child as soon as she gave birth. (12:4).
And she gave birth to a son, a male child, who will rule all the nations with an iron scepter. And her child was caught up to God and to His throne. (12:5).
And the woman fled into the wilderness, where God had prepared a place for her to be nourished for 1,260 days. (12:6).
Then a war broke out in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back. (12:7).
But the dragon was not strong enough, and no longer was any place found in heaven for him and his angels. (12:8).
And the great dragon was hurled down — that ancient serpent called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world. He was hurled to the earth, and his angels with him. (12:9).

And I heard a loud voice in heaven saying: “Now have come the salvation and the power and the kingdom of our God, and the authority of His Christ. For the accuser of our brothers has been thrown down — he who accuses them day and night before our God. (12:10).
They have conquered him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony. And they did not love their lives so as to shy away from death. (12:11).
Therefore rejoice, O heavens, and you who dwell in them! But woe to the earth and the sea; with great fury the devil has come down to you, knowing he has only a short time.” (12:12).
And when the dragon saw that he had been thrown to the earth, he pursued the woman who had given birth to the male child. (12:13).
But the woman was given two wings of a great eagle to fly from the presence of the serpent to her place in the wilderness, where she was nourished for a time, and times, and half a time. (12:14).
Then from his mouth the serpent spewed water like a river to overtake the woman and sweep her away in the torrent. (12:15).
But the earth helped the woman and opened its mouth to swallow up the river that the dragon had poured from his mouth. (12:16).

And the dragon was enraged at the woman and went to make war with the rest of her children, who keep the commandments of God and hold to the testimony of Jesus. And the dragon stood on the shore of the sea. (12:17).
crossRefs: Genesis 3:15: Enmity between woman’s seed and serpent.
Psalm 2:9: Rule with rod of iron.
Daniel 7:25: Time, times, and half a time.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שֵׁבֶט בַּרְזֶל (šēḇeṭ barzel), Greek: ῥάβδῳ σιδηρᾷ (rhábdō sidēra, NT), Aramaic: שבטא דפרזלא (šeḇṭā d-parzelā)
translationNotes.note: Symbol of firm, unbreakable rule associated with Messiah.

translationNotes.term: Time, times, and half a time
translationNotes.original: Greek: καιρὸν καὶ καιροὺς καὶ ἥμισυ καιροῦ (kairon kai kairous kai hemisu kairou) - Aramaic: עִדָּן וְעִדָּנִין וּפְלַג עִדָּן (iddan we-iddanin u-felag iddan)
translationNotes.note: Symbolic period of three and a half years, matching 1,260 days and forty-two months.

translationNotes.original: Greek: δράκων (drakōn)
translationNotes.note: Identified explicitly as the devil, Satan, and the ancient serpent from Genesis.

stories.keyTakeaway: John sees a vision of a woman, her child caught up to God, and the dragon defeated in heaven but warring against her offspring on earth.

stories.title: 🌿 Revelation 13
summaryBullets: Then I saw a beast with ten horns and seven heads rising out of the sea. There were ten royal crowns on its horns and blasphemous names on its heads. (13:1).
The beast I saw was like a leopard, with the feet of a bear and the mouth of a lion. And the dragon gave the beast his power and his throne and great authority. (13:2).
One of the heads of the beast appeared to have been mortally wounded. But the mortal wound was healed, and the whole world marveled and followed the beast. (13:3).
They worshiped the dragon who had given authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast, saying, “Who is like the beast, and who can wage war against it?” (13:4).
The beast was given a mouth to speak arrogant and blasphemous words, and authority to act for 42 months. (13:5).
And the beast opened its mouth to speak blasphemies against God and to slander His name and His tabernacle — those who dwell in heaven. (13:6).
Then the beast was permitted to wage war against the saints and to conquer them, and it was given authority over every tribe and people and tongue and nation. (13:7).
And all who dwell on the earth will worship the beast — all whose names have not been written from the foundation of the world in the Book of Life belonging to the Lamb who was slain. (13:8).
He who has an ear, let him hear: (13:9).

“If anyone is destined for captivity, into captivity he will go; if anyone is to die by the sword, by the sword he must be killed.” Here is a call for the perseverance and faith of the saints. (13:10).
Then I saw another beast rising out of the earth. This beast had two horns like a lamb, but spoke like a dragon. (13:11).
And this beast exercised all the authority of the first beast and caused the earth and those who dwell in it to worship the first beast, whose mortal wound had been healed. (13:12).
And the second beast performed great signs, even causing fire from heaven to come down to earth in the presence of the people. (13:13).

Because of the signs it was given to perform on behalf of the first beast, it deceived those who dwell on the earth, telling them to make an image to the beast that had been wounded by the sword and yet had lived. (13:14).
The second beast was permitted to give breath to the image of the first beast, so that the image could speak and cause all who refused to worship it to be killed. (13:15).
And the second beast required all people, small and great, rich and poor, free and slave, to receive a mark on their right hand or on their forehead, (13:16).
so that no one could buy or sell unless he had the mark — the name of the beast or the number of its name. (13:17).
Here is a call for wisdom: Let the one who has insight calculate the number of the beast, for it is the number of a man, and that number is 666. (13:18).
crossRefs: Daniel 7:3-8: Four beasts rising from sea.
Daniel 3:5-6: Image to be worshiped under threat of death.
2 Thessalonians 2:9: Signs and wonders of lawless one.

translationNotes.original: Greek: χάραγμα (charagma)
translationNotes.note: Charagma is not a vague sign. It is the technical word for something stamped or engraved: the imprint of a die on a coin, the official stamp certifying a document, a brand burned into a slave or an animal. It is placed on the right hand or the forehead (13:16), the two places nobody can hide, and 13:17 ties it to the right to buy or sell. Acts 17:29 uses the same word for the engraved work of an idol.

translationNotes.original: Greek: χξϛ (chi, xi, stigma) = 600 + 60 + 6
translationNotes.note: Greek had no separate digits. The alphabet did double duty, so the number in 13:18 stands in the manuscripts as three letters, chi xi stigma. Because every name was therefore also a sum, people played with it: a wall at Pompeii carries the line 'I love her whose number is 545'. That letter arithmetic is what 'let the one who has understanding calculate' refers to, and the text supplies the total rather than the name.

translationNotes.term: The image that was given breath
translationNotes.original: Greek: εἰκών τοῦ θηρίου (eikon tou theriou, image of the beast)
translationNotes.note: An eikon is a statue or portrait, and compulsory reverence toward one was a real civic instrument in the province these letters go to. Pergamum built the first temple in Asia to Rome and Augustus in 29 BC, Smyrna won one for Tiberius in AD 26, and refusing the required gesture at such a temple was treated as disloyalty rather than as a private belief. Daniel 3:5-6 is the older version of the same demand: bow at the sound of the music or go into the furnace.

translationNotes.term: Two beasts, and what the second is called later
translationNotes.original: Greek: θηρίον (therion, wild beast)
translationNotes.note: Verse 1 has a beast come up out of the sea; verse 11 has a second come up out of the earth, with two horns like a lamb and the voice of a dragon. This second one is the one that makes the image, works signs, and enforces the mark. Later in the book it is called by a different name, the false prophet (16:13; 19:20; 20:10), which is the text's own identification.

translationNotes.original: Greek: μῆνας τεσσεράκοντα δύο (menas tesserakonta dyo)
translationNotes.note: Three and a half years, expressed three different ways across these chapters: forty-two months here and at 11:2, 1,260 days at 11:3 and 12:6, and a time, times and half a time at 12:14. Daniel uses the same span (Daniel 7:25; 12:7). It is a period with a stated limit, counted from its start.

stories.keyTakeaway: John sees a beast from sea and another from earth empowered by dragon, demanding worship, persecuting saints, and marking followers with 666.

stories.title: 🕊️ Revelation 14
summaryBullets: Then I looked and saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with Him 144,000 who had His name and His Father’s name written on their foreheads. (14:1).
And I heard a sound from heaven like the roar of many waters and the loud rumbling of thunder. And the sound I heard was like harpists strumming their harps. (14:2).
And they sang a new song before the throne and before the four living creatures and the elders. And no one could learn the song except the 144,000 who had been redeemed from the earth. (14:3).

These are the ones who have not been defiled with women, for they are virgins. They follow the Lamb wherever He goes. They have been redeemed from among men as firstfruits to God and to the Lamb. (14:4).
And no lie was found in their mouths; they are blameless. (14:5).
Then I saw another angel flying overhead, with the eternal gospel to proclaim to those who dwell on the earth — to every nation and tribe and tongue and people. (14:6).

And he said in a loud voice, “Fear God and give Him glory, because the hour of His judgment has come. Worship the One who made the heavens and the earth and the sea and the springs of waters.” (14:7).
Then a second angel followed, saying, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great, who has made all the nations drink the wine of the passion of her immorality.” (14:8).
And a third angel followed them, calling out in a loud voice, “If anyone worships the beast and its image and receives its mark on his forehead or on his hand, (14:9).
he too will drink the wine of God’s anger, poured undiluted into the cup of His wrath. And he will be tormented in fire and sulfur in the presence of the holy angels and of the Lamb. (14:10).
And the smoke of their torment rises forever and ever. Day and night there is no rest for those who worship the beast and its image, or for anyone who receives the mark of its name.” (14:11).
Here is a call for the perseverance of the saints, who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus. (14:12).

And I heard a voice from heaven telling me to write, “Blessed are the dead — those who die in the Lord from this moment on.” “Yes,” says the Spirit, “they will rest from their labors, for their deeds will follow them.” (14:13).
And I looked and saw a white cloud, and seated on the cloud was One like the Son of Man, with a golden crown on His head and a sharp sickle in His hand. (14:14).

Then another angel came out of the temple, crying out in a loud voice to the One seated on the cloud, “Swing Your sickle and reap, because the time has come to harvest, for the crop of the earth is ripe.” (14:15).
So the One seated on the cloud swung His sickle over the earth, and the earth was harvested. (14:16).
Then another angel came out of the temple in heaven, and he too had a sharp sickle. (14:17).

Still another angel, with authority over the fire, came from the altar and called out in a loud voice to the angel with the sharp sickle, “Swing your sharp sickle and gather the clusters of grapes from the vine of the earth, because its grapes are ripe.” (14:18).
So the angel swung his sickle over the earth and gathered the grapes of the earth, and he threw them into the great winepress of God’s wrath. (14:19).
And the winepress was trodden outside the city, and the blood that flowed from it rose as high as the bridles of the horses for a distance of 1,600 stadia. (14:20).
crossRefs: Joel 3:13: Put in the sickle, harvest is ripe.
Isaiah 63:3: Winepress of wrath.
Matthew 24:30: Son of Man on clouds.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ληνός (lenos) - Hebrew: גַּת (gat)
translationNotes.note: A winepress was a shallow floor cut into rock with a channel running to a lower catch basin. Men trod the grapes barefoot, holding ropes or a beam overhead, and the juice ran out of the channel and splashed dark red up the legs and clothing. Isaiah 63:1-3 uses exactly that picture, one man treading alone with his garments stained. That is the image behind 14:19-20, and it is a work scene before it is anything else.

translationNotes.original: Greek: στάδιον (stadion)
translationNotes.note: A stadion is about 607 feet, 185 metres, and eight of them make roughly a Roman mile. Sixteen hundred stadia is therefore about 184 miles, or 296 kilometres, which is a distance in the same range as the length of the land of Israel. The measure of depth in 14:20 is given as up to the horses' bridles.

translationNotes.original: Greek: δρέπανον (drepanon)
translationNotes.note: A short curved blade on a wooden handle, swung one-handed close to the ground while the other hand gathered the stalks; the same tool cut grain and cut grape clusters. Joel 3:13 is the line being used here: put in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe, go in and tread, for the winepress is full. Two harvests are described in 14:14-20, grain first and grapes second.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἀπαρχή (aparche) - Hebrew: בִּכּוּרִים (bikkurim)
translationNotes.note: The first portion of a harvest, brought to God before any of the rest could be used (Exodus 23:19; Leviticus 23:9-14). Calling something firstfruits says two things at once: it is the best, and there is more of the same crop coming. Paul calls the risen Christ the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep (1 Corinthians 15:20).

translationNotes.original: Greek: Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη (Babylon he megale)
translationNotes.note: The first mention in this book, announced by the second angel as fallen (14:8) in the words of Isaiah 21:9. The city is not described here at all; chapters 17 and 18 do that. What 14:8 says of her is that she made all nations drink the wine of the passion of her immorality.

stories.keyTakeaway: John sees Lamb with 144,000, three angels’ messages of gospel, Babylon’s fall, and wrath against beast worshipers, followed by harvest of earth.

headings.text: The Three Angels and Babylon’s Fall

stories.title: 📜 Revelation 15
summaryBullets: Then I saw another great and marvelous sign in heaven: seven angels with the seven final plagues, with which the wrath of God is completed. (15:1).
And I saw something like a sea of glass mixed with fire, beside which stood those who had conquered the beast and its image and the number of its name. They were holding harps from God, (15:2).
and they sang the song of God’s servant Moses and of the Lamb: “Great and wonderful are Your works, O Lord God Almighty! Just and true are Your ways, O King of the nations! (15:3).
