Who will not fear You, O Lord, and glorify Your name? For You alone are holy. All nations will come and worship before You, for Your righteous acts have been revealed.” (15:4).
After this I looked, and the temple — the tabernacle of the Testimony — was opened in heaven. (15:5).
And out of the temple came the seven angels with the seven plagues, dressed in clean and bright linen and girded with golden sashes around their chests. (15:6).
Then one of the four living creatures gave the seven angels seven golden bowls full of the wrath of God, who lives forever and ever. (15:7).
And the temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God and from His power; and no one could enter the temple until the seven plagues of the seven angels were completed. (15:8).
crossRefs: Exodus 15:1-18: The song Moses and Israel sang at the sea after the LORD threw horse and rider into it.
Deuteronomy 32:3-4: Ascribe greatness to our God; His work is perfect, and all His ways are justice.
Psalm 86:8-10: All the nations You have made shall come and worship before You and glorify Your name.
Numbers 9:15-16: The cloud covers the tabernacle of the testimony by day and the appearance of fire by night.
Exodus 40:34-35: The glory of the LORD fills the tabernacle and Moses cannot enter it.

translationNotes.term: The song of Moses and of the Lamb
translationNotes.original: Greek: ᾠδὴν Μωϋσέως (oden Mouseos, song of Moses)
translationNotes.note: Israel sang at the sea after Egypt's chariots went down in it (Exodus 15:1-18), and Moses left a second song before his death (Deuteronomy 32). The words given in 15:3-4 are drawn from those and from the psalms: great and marvellous are Your works, just and true are Your ways, all nations will come and worship. The singers in 15:2 are the ones who came through the beast, standing beside a sea of glass mixed with fire.

translationNotes.original: Greek: πληγή (plege, a blow or stroke)
translationNotes.note: The Greek word means a blow struck, and by extension the wound it leaves. The Septuagint uses it of what fell on Egypt, which is why English Bibles say plagues. Verse 1 calls these seven the last, because with them the wrath of God is finished.

translationNotes.original: Greek: φιάλη (phiale) - Hebrew: מִזְרָק (mizraq)
translationNotes.note: A phiale is a wide shallow dish with no handles, the shape used for pouring out a libation; the temple equivalent is the mizraq, the basin the priests used to dash blood against the altar (Exodus 27:3). The shape matters: a bowl is emptied in one motion. Seals were broken one at a time and trumpets sounded in sequence; these are tipped over.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ὁ ναὸς τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου (ho naos tes skenes tou martyriou)
translationNotes.note: The tabernacle was called the tent of the testimony because it housed the ark containing the two stone tablets, which are the testimony (Exodus 25:16; Numbers 9:15; 17:7-8). The name says the structure exists to hold the evidence of a covenant. Verse 5 opens that sanctuary in heaven, and the seven angels come out of it.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἐγεμίσθη ὁ ναὸς καπνοῦ (egemisthe ho naos kapnou)
translationNotes.note: Verse 8 says no one could enter the sanctuary until the seven plagues were finished. That has happened twice before in Scripture: the cloud filled the tabernacle so Moses could not go in (Exodus 40:34-35), and it filled the temple so the priests could not stand to minister (1 Kings 8:10-11). Isaiah 6:4 has the house fill with smoke as the seraphim call.

stories.keyTakeaway: Seven angels holding the final plagues appear in heaven; those who overcame the beast sing praise beside a sea of glass while the temple opens and the angels receive golden bowls filled with God's wrath.

headings.text: The Song of Moses and the Lamb

stories.title: 🌿 Revelation 16
summaryBullets: Then I heard a loud voice from the temple saying to the seven angels, “Go, pour out on the earth the seven bowls of God’s wrath.” (16:1).
So the first angel went and poured out his bowl on the earth, and loathsome, malignant sores broke out on those who had the mark of the beast and worshiped its image. (16:2).
And the second angel poured out his bowl into the sea, and it turned to blood like that of the dead, and every living thing in the sea died. (16:3).
And the third angel poured out his bowl into the rivers and springs of water, and they turned to blood. (16:4).
And I heard the angel of the waters say: “Righteous are You, O Holy One, who is and was, because You have brought these judgments. (16:5).
For they have spilled the blood of saints and prophets, and You have given them blood to drink, as they deserve.” (16:6).
And I heard the altar reply: “Yes, Lord God Almighty, true and just are Your judgments.” (16:7).
Then the fourth angel poured out his bowl on the sun, and it was given power to scorch the people with fire. (16:8).
And the people were scorched by intense heat, and they cursed the name of God, who had authority over these plagues. Yet they did not repent and give Him glory. (16:9).
And the fifth angel poured out his bowl on the throne of the beast, and its kingdom was plunged into darkness, and men began to gnaw their tongues in anguish (16:10).
and curse the God of heaven for their pains and sores. Yet they did not repent of their deeds. (16:11).
And the sixth angel poured out his bowl on the great river Euphrates, and its water was dried up to prepare the way for the kings of the East. (16:12).
And I saw three unclean spirits that looked like frogs coming out of the mouths of the dragon, the beast, and the false prophet. (16:13).
These are demonic spirits that perform signs and go out to all the kings of the earth, to assemble them for battle on the great day of God the Almighty. (16:14).
[J]“Behold, I am coming like a thief. Blessed is the one who remains awake and clothed, so that he will not go naked and let his shame be exposed.”[/J] (16:15).
And they assembled the kings in the place that in Hebrew is called Armageddon. (16:16).
Then the seventh angel poured out his bowl into the air, and a loud voice came from the throne in the temple, saying, “It is done!” (16:17).
And there were flashes of lightning, rumblings, peals of thunder, and a great earthquake the likes of which had not occurred since men were upon the earth — so mighty was the great quake. (16:18).
The great city was split into three parts, and the cities of the nations collapsed. And God remembered Babylon the great and gave her the cup of the wine of the fury of His wrath. (16:19).
Then every island fled, and no mountain could be found. (16:20).
And great hailstones weighing almost a hundred pounds each rained down on them from above. And men cursed God for the plague of hail, because it was so horrendous. (16:21).
crossRefs: Exodus 7:20-21: The water of the Nile turns to blood, the fish die, and the river stinks.
Exodus 8:1-6: Frogs come up out of the Nile and cover the land, going into the houses, the beds and the ovens.
Exodus 9:8-11: Soot thrown toward heaven becomes boils breaking out on man and beast throughout Egypt.
Judges 5:19-21: Kings came and fought at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo, and the torrent Kishon swept them away.
2 Kings 23:29-30: Josiah goes out to meet Pharaoh Neco and is killed at Megiddo, and they carry him back to Jerusalem.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἕλκος (helkos)
translationNotes.note: Helkos is an open ulcer or running sore. It is the exact word the Septuagint uses for the boils that broke out on the Egyptians (Exodus 9:9-11) and for the sores that covered Job (Job 2:7), and Luke 16:21 uses it of the beggar Lazarus. Verse 2 puts them on the people who carry the mark.

translationNotes.original: Greek: Εὐφράτης (Euphrates) - Hebrew: פְּרָת (Perat)
translationNotes.note: The great river of Mesopotamia, about 1,700 miles long, and the eastern boundary of the land promised to Abraham (Genesis 15:18) as well as the eastern frontier of the Roman world, with Parthia beyond it. Drying a river is how Babylon fell the first time: Herodotus (1.191) says Cyrus diverted the Euphrates and his troops walked in along the riverbed. Isaiah 44:27 and Jeremiah 50:38 both speak of her waters being dried up.

translationNotes.original: Greek: βάτραχοι (batrachoi)
translationNotes.note: The second plague on Egypt, when frogs came up out of the river into the houses, the beds and the kneading bowls, and Pharaoh's magicians did the same thing (Exodus 8:1-7). Frogs are among the creatures the Law declares unclean, being water creatures without fins or scales (Leviticus 11:9-12). Verse 13 says three unclean spirits like frogs come out of the mouths of the dragon, the beast and the false prophet.

translationNotes.original: Greek: Ἁρμαγεδών (Harmagedon) - Hebrew: הַר מְגִדּוֹ (har Megiddo, mount of Megiddo)
translationNotes.note: Megiddo is a real mound in the Jezreel valley, about twenty miles southeast of modern Haifa, guarding the narrow pass where the highway between Egypt and Mesopotamia squeezes through the Carmel ridge. Whoever held it controlled the road, so armies fought for it for three thousand years: Thutmose III took it in the fifteenth century BC, Deborah and Barak fought there (Judges 5:19), and Josiah was killed there by Pharaoh Neco (2 Kings 23:29). Excavation has found more than twenty layers of successive cities stacked on the site.

translationNotes.original: Greek: χάλαζα μεγάλη ὡς ταλαντιαία (chalaza megale hos talantiaia)
translationNotes.note: A talent is roughly 75 pounds, 34 kilograms, so 16:21 is describing hail the weight of a full grain sack. Hail was a recognised weapon of God in Scripture: it broke Egypt (Exodus 9:23-25), and at Beth-horon more of the enemy died from the hailstones than from Israel's swords (Joshua 10:11).

stories.keyTakeaway: Seven angels pour out bowls of God's wrath on earth: sores on the marked, blood in sea and waters, scorching sun, darkness over the beast's kingdom, dried Euphrates, and demonic spirits gathering kings to Armageddon; the seventh bowl brings catastrophic earthquake, collapse of cities, and massive hailstones.

headings.text: The First Six Bowls of Wrath

stories.title: 📜 Revelation 17
summaryBullets: Then one of the seven angels with the seven bowls came and said to me, “Come, I will show you the punishment of the great prostitute, who sits on many waters. (17:1).
The kings of the earth were immoral with her, and those who dwell on the earth were intoxicated with the wine of her immorality.” (17:2).
And the angel carried me away in the Spirit into a wilderness, where I saw a woman sitting on a scarlet beast that was covered with blasphemous names and had seven heads and ten horns. (17:3).

The woman was dressed in purple and scarlet, and adorned with gold and precious stones and pearls. She held in her hand a golden cup full of abominations and the impurities of her sexual immorality. (17:4).
And on her forehead a mysterious name was written: BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF PROSTITUTES AND OF THE ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH. (17:5).
I could see that the woman was drunk with the blood of the saints and witnesses for Jesus. And I was utterly amazed at the sight of her. (17:6).
“Why are you so amazed?” said the angel. “I will tell you the mystery of the woman and of the beast that carries her, which has the seven heads and ten horns. (17:7).

The beast that you saw — it was, and now is no more, but is about to come up out of the Abyss and go to its destruction. And those who dwell on the earth whose names were not written in the Book of Life from the foundation of the world will marvel when they see the beast that was, and is not, and yet will be. (17:8).
This calls for a mind with wisdom. The seven heads are seven mountains on which the woman sits. (17:9).
There are also seven kings. Five have fallen, one is, and the other has not yet come. But when he does come, he must remain for only a little while. (17:10).
The beast that was, and now is not, is an eighth king, who belongs to the other seven and is going into destruction. (17:11).
The ten horns you saw are ten kings who have not yet received a kingdom, but will receive one hour of authority as kings along with the beast. (17:12).
These kings have one purpose: to yield their power and authority to the beast. (17:13).

They will make war against the Lamb, and the Lamb will triumph over them, because He is Lord of lords and King of kings; and He will be accompanied by His called and chosen and faithful ones.” (17:14).
Then the angel said to me, “The waters you saw, where the prostitute was seated, are peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues. (17:15).
And the ten horns and the beast that you saw will hate the prostitute. They will leave her desolate and naked, and they will eat her flesh and burn her with fire. (17:16).
For God has put it into their hearts to carry out His purpose by uniting to give their kingdom to the beast, until the words of God are fulfilled. (17:17).
And the woman you saw is the great city that rules over the kings of the earth.” (17:18).
crossRefs: Jeremiah 51:6-13: Babylon was a golden cup in the LORD's hand, making all the earth drunk, and she dwells by many waters.
Isaiah 23:15-17: Tyre is treated as a forgotten prostitute who plies her trade with all the kingdoms of the world.
Nahum 3:1-5: The bloody city, mistress of sorceries, is stripped and shown to the nations.
Zechariah 5:5-11: A woman is shut in a basket and carried off to the land of Shinar, where a house is built for her.
Daniel 7:19-25: The fourth beast has ten horns, which are ten kings, and another rises after them and subdues three.

translationNotes.term: Babylon as the name of a city
translationNotes.original: Greek: Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη (Babylon he megale)
translationNotes.note: Babylon on the Euphrates was the empire that burned the temple in 586 BC, and by the time John wrote it was a ruin; Strabo, a generation earlier, wrote that the great city had become a great desert. Revelation states plainly what it means by the name: the woman is the great city that rules over the kings of the earth (17:18), and she sits on seven mountains (17:9). Peter closes his first letter with greetings from 'she who is in Babylon' (1 Peter 5:13).

translationNotes.original: Greek: πορφυροῦν καὶ κόκκινον (porphyroun kai kokkinon)
translationNotes.note: The two most expensive colours in the ancient world. Purple and violet came from the murex sea snail, thousands of shells crushed for a few grams of dye; scarlet came from the kermes insect. Diocletian's price edict of AD 301 caps purple-dyed silk at 150,000 denarii a pound in a document that sets a farm labourer's daily wage at 25 denarii. Verse 4 is describing an outfit worth more than a working life.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ποτήριον χρυσοῦν (poterion chrysoun)
translationNotes.note: Jeremiah 51:7 says Babylon was a golden cup in the LORD's hand that made all the earth drunk, and the cup of wrath which the nations must drink runs through the prophets (Jeremiah 25:15-17; Isaiah 51:17). Verse 4 puts a gold cup in her hand and says what it holds. The vessel is beautiful and the contents are not.

translationNotes.term: The book interprets its own symbols here
translationNotes.original: Greek: ὧδε ὁ νοῦς ὁ ἔχων σοφίαν (hode ho nous ho echon sophian, here is the mind that has wisdom)
translationNotes.note: This chapter is the one place where the angel stops and explains: the seven heads are seven mountains and also seven kings (17:9-10), the ten horns are ten kings who have not yet received a kingdom (17:12), the waters are peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues (17:15), and the woman is the great city (17:18). Where the text supplies its own key, no other key is needed.

translationNotes.original: Greek: μισήσουσιν τὴν πόρνην (misesousin ten pornen, they will hate the prostitute)
translationNotes.note: Verses 16-17 say the beast and the ten horns will hate the woman, strip her, eat her flesh and burn her with fire, and that God put it into their hearts to do it until His words are fulfilled. The alliance destroys itself. That is the sequence the chapter sets up before chapter 18 sings the funeral.

stories.keyTakeaway: An angel shows John a woman called Babylon the Great sitting on a scarlet beast with seven heads and ten horns; the angel interprets the vision, explaining that the seven heads are seven kings and the ten horns are ten kings who will wage war against the Lamb but will ultimately be defeated. The beast and ten horns will destroy the prostitute, and God will use them to accomplish his purpose before their destruction.

stories.title: 🌿 Revelation 18
summaryBullets: After this I saw another angel descending from heaven with great authority, and the earth was illuminated by his glory. (18:1).

And he cried out in a mighty voice: “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great! She has become a lair for demons and a haunt for every unclean spirit, every unclean bird, and every detestable beast. (18:2).

All the nations have drunk the wine of the passion of her immorality. The kings of the earth were immoral with her, and the merchants of the earth have grown wealthy from the extravagance of her luxury.” (18:3).
Then I heard another voice from heaven say: “Come out of her, My people, so that you will not share in her sins or contract any of her plagues. (18:4).
For her sins are piled up to heaven, and God has remembered her iniquities. (18:5).
Give back to her as she has done to others; pay her back double for what she has done; mix her a double portion in her own cup. (18:6).
As much as she has glorified herself and lived in luxury, give her the same measure of torment and grief. In her heart she says, ‘I sit as queen; I am not a widow and will never see grief.’ (18:7).
Therefore her plagues will come in one day — death and grief and famine — and she will be consumed by fire, for mighty is the Lord God who judges her.” (18:8).
Then the kings of the earth who committed sexual immorality and lived in luxury with her will weep and wail at the sight of the smoke rising from the fire that consumes her. (18:9).
In fear of her torment, they will stand at a distance and cry out: “Woe, woe to the great city, the mighty city of Babylon! For in a single hour your judgment has come.” (18:10).
And the merchants of the earth will weep and mourn over her, because there is no one left to buy their cargo — (18:11).
cargo of gold, silver, precious stones, and pearls; of fine linen, purple, silk, and scarlet; of all kinds of citron wood and every article of ivory, precious wood, bronze, iron, and marble; (18:12).
of cinnamon, spice, incense, myrrh, and frankincense; of wine, olive oil, fine flour, and wheat; of cattle, sheep, horses, and carriages; of bodies and souls of slaves. (18:13).
And they will say: “The fruit of your soul’s desire has departed from you; all your luxury and splendor have vanished, never to be seen again.” (18:14).
The merchants who sold these things and gained their wealth from her will stand at a distance, in fear of her torment. They will weep and mourn, (18:15).
saying: “Woe, woe to the great city, clothed in fine linen and purple and scarlet, adorned with gold and precious stones and pearls! (18:16).
For in a single hour such fabulous wealth has been destroyed!” Every shipmaster, passenger, and sailor, and all who make their living from the sea, will stand at a distance (18:17).
and cry out at the sight of the smoke rising from the fire that consumes her. “What city was ever like this great city?” they will exclaim. (18:18).

Then they will throw dust on their heads as they weep and mourn and cry out: “Woe, woe to the great city, where all who had ships on the sea were enriched by her wealth! For in a single hour she has been destroyed.” (18:19).
Rejoice over her, O heaven, and you saints and apostles and prophets, because God has pronounced for you His judgment against her. (18:20).
Then a mighty angel picked up a stone the size of a great millstone and cast it into the sea, saying: “With such violence the great city of Babylon will be cast down, never to be seen again. (18:21).

And the sound of harpists and musicians, of flute players and trumpeters, will never ring out in you again. Nor will any craftsmen of any trade be found in you again, nor the sound of a millstone be heard in you again. (18:22).

The light of a lamp will never shine in you again, and the voices of a bride and bridegroom will never call out in you again. For your merchants were the great ones of the earth, because all the nations were deceived by your sorcery.” (18:23).
And there was found in her the blood of prophets and saints, and of all who had been slain on the earth. (18:24).
crossRefs: Isaiah 13:19-22: Babylon will be like Sodom, never inhabited again, with desert creatures lying in her houses.
Isaiah 47:7-11: The queen who says she will never sit as a widow loses children and widowhood in one day.
Jeremiah 25:9-11: The LORD will banish from them the sound of the millstones and the light of the lamp.
Jeremiah 51:59-64: Seraiah reads the scroll of judgment, ties a stone to it, and throws it into the Euphrates.
Ezekiel 27:25-36: The ships of Tarshish carried Tyre's cargo, and the mariners stand off from her wreck and wail.

translationNotes.original: Greek: γόμος (gomos, a ship's cargo)
translationNotes.note: Verses 12-13 are a working manifest of the Roman luxury trade, in descending order of value: gold, silver, gems and pearls; fine linen, purple, silk and scarlet; citron wood, ivory, costly wood, bronze, iron and marble; cinnamon, spice, incense, myrrh and frankincense; wine, oil, fine flour and wheat; cattle, sheep, horses and carriages. Silk came overland from China and cost a fortune. Citron wood from North Africa was cut into table tops, and Pliny records single tables selling for the price of a large estate.

translationNotes.term: Bodies, that is, souls of men
translationNotes.original: Greek: σωμάτων, καὶ ψυχὰς ἀνθρώπων (somaton, kai psychas anthropon)
translationNotes.note: The last item on the manifest is slaves. Somata, bodies, was the ordinary commercial term for them in Greek business documents, the way a modern bill of lading says units. The text writes the trade word and then refuses to leave it there, adding 'and souls of men'.

translationNotes.term: A stone like a great millstone
translationNotes.original: Greek: λίθον ὡς μύλινον μέγαν (lithon hos mylinon megan)
translationNotes.note: Household mills used two small stones a woman could turn by hand. A commercial mill was turned by a donkey and its upper stone was cut from hard volcanic rock, waist high and weighing several hundred pounds; whole examples still stand in the bakeries of Pompeii. That is the stone Jesus names in Matthew 18:6, and the one thrown into the sea here.

translationNotes.original: Greek: μιᾷ ὥρᾳ (mia hora)
translationNotes.note: The phrase is repeated three times in the mourning songs, by the kings, the merchants and the shipmasters (18:10, 17, 19). Beside it stands 'in one day' at 18:8. The complaint of all three groups is not that judgment came but that it came too fast to move anything out.

translationNotes.term: Standing far off, throwing dust on their heads
translationNotes.original: Greek: ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἑστηκότες (apo makrothen hestekotes)
translationNotes.note: Every group in the chapter mourns from a distance and none of them helps. Throwing dust or earth on the head was the standard act of grief (Joshua 7:6; Job 2:12; Lamentations 2:10), and Ezekiel 27:30-32 has the mariners of Tyre do exactly this over her wreck. The scene here is written on the pattern of that older lament.

translationNotes.term: No lamp, no millstone, no bridegroom
translationNotes.original: Greek: φωνὴ μύλου (phone mylou, the sound of a mill)
translationNotes.note: Verses 22-23 list what will not be heard again: harpists, musicians, flute players and trumpeters, any craftsman at his trade, the sound of a mill, the light of a lamp, the voice of bride and bridegroom. Those are the ordinary sounds of a town at work in the morning and at rest in the evening. Jeremiah 25:10 uses the same short list for the silence that falls on a destroyed city.

stories.keyTakeaway: An angel announces Babylon's fall; the kings and merchants who grew wealthy through her mourn her destruction, while those in heaven rejoice that God has judged her for her sins and the blood of prophets found within her.

stories.title: 🕊️ Revelation 19
summaryBullets: After this I heard a sound like the roar of a great multitude in heaven, shouting: “Hallelujah! Salvation and glory and power belong to our God! (19:1).
For His judgments are true and just. He has judged the great prostitute who corrupted the earth with her immorality. He has avenged the blood of His servants that was poured out by her hand.” (19:2).
And a second time they called out: “Hallelujah! Her smoke rises forever and ever.” (19:3).
And the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshiped God who sits on the throne, saying: “Amen, Hallelujah!” (19:4).
Then a voice came from the throne, saying: “Praise our God, all you who serve Him, and those who fear Him, small and great alike!” (19:5).

And I heard a sound like the roar of a great multitude, like the rushing of many waters, and like a mighty rumbling of thunder, crying out: “Hallelujah! For the Lord our God the Almighty reigns. (19:6).
Let us rejoice and be glad and give Him the glory. For the marriage of the Lamb has come, and His bride has made herself ready. (19:7).
She was given clothing of fine linen, bright and pure.” For the fine linen she wears is the righteous acts of the saints. (19:8).
Then the angel told me to write, “Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.” And he said to me, “These are the true words of God.” (19:9).

So I fell at his feet to worship him. But he told me, “Do not do that! I am a fellow servant with you and your brothers who rely on the testimony of Jesus. Worship God! For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.” (19:10).
Then I saw heaven standing open, and there before me was a white horse. And its rider is called Faithful and True. With righteousness He judges and wages war. (19:11).
He has eyes like blazing fire, and many royal crowns on His head. He has a name written on Him that only He Himself knows. (19:12).
He is dressed in a robe dipped in blood, and His name is The Word of God. (19:13).
The armies of heaven, dressed in fine linen, white and pure, follow Him on white horses. (19:14).

And from His mouth proceeds a sharp sword with which to strike down the nations, and He will rule them with an iron scepter. He treads the winepress of the fury of the wrath of God the Almighty. (19:15).
And He has a name written on His robe and on His thigh: KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS. (19:16).
Then I saw an angel standing in the sun, and he cried out in a loud voice to all the birds flying overhead, “Come, gather together for the great supper of God, (19:17).
so that you may eat the flesh of kings and commanders and mighty men, of horses and riders, of everyone slave and free, small and great.” (19:18).
Then I saw the beast and the kings of the earth with their armies assembled to wage war against the One seated on the horse, and against His army. (19:19).

But the beast was captured along with the false prophet, who on its behalf had performed signs deceiving those who had the mark of the beast and worshiped its image. Both the beast and the false prophet were thrown alive into the fiery lake of burning sulfur. (19:20).
And the rest were killed with the sword that proceeded from the mouth of the One seated on the horse. And all the birds gorged themselves on their flesh. (19:21).
crossRefs: Psalm 45:3-5: Gird your sword on your thigh, O mighty one, and ride out victoriously for truth and righteousness.
Isaiah 11:4: He shall strike the earth with the rod of His mouth, and with the breath of His lips slay the wicked.
Deuteronomy 10:17: The LORD your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, the mighty and the awesome.
Ezekiel 39:17-20: Birds and beasts are summoned to a sacrificial feast to eat the flesh of the mighty and drink the blood of princes.
Matthew 22:1-14: A king gives a wedding feast for his son, sends out his servants, and inspects the guests' clothing.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הַלְלוּ־יָהּ (hallelu-Yah, praise Yah) - Greek: Ἁλληλουϊά (Hallelouia)
translationNotes.note: A Hebrew imperative, praise, joined to the shortened form of the divine name. It opens and closes many psalms, especially the block of Psalms 146 to 150 where it stands at both ends of every one. Revelation 19:1, 3, 4 and 6 are the only four occurrences of the word in the New Testament, and they all fall in these six verses.

translationNotes.original: Greek: βύσσινον λαμπρὸν καθαρόν (byssinon lampron katharon)
translationNotes.note: Byssos is the expensive bleached linen of Egypt, the cloth used for priestly garments and for the rich man's clothing in Luke 16:19. It appears twice in this chapter, on the bride (19:8) and on the armies following the rider (19:14). Verse 8 states what it stands for and leaves nothing to guess: the righteous deeds of the saints.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἱμάτιον βεβαμμένον αἵματι (himation bebammenon haimati)
translationNotes.note: The robe is already stained when the rider appears, before any battle in the chapter is fought. Isaiah 63:1-3 is the passage in view: someone comes from Edom with crimson garments because he has trodden the winepress alone and their lifeblood spattered his clothes. Verse 15 names the same winepress.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ῥομφαία (rhomphaia)
translationNotes.note: Two Greek words are translated sword. The machaira is the short blade a soldier or a butcher carried; the rhomphaia is a long broad Thracian sword, the one used in this book (1:16; 2:12; 19:15, 21). It comes out of His mouth, not His hand, which matches Isaiah 11:4, where He strikes the earth with the rod of His mouth.

translationNotes.term: King of kings and Lord of lords
translationNotes.original: Greek: βασιλεὺς βασιλέων καὶ κύριος κυρίων (basileus basileon kai kyrios kyrion)
translationNotes.note: King of kings was the formal title of the great kings of the East, claimed by Babylonian and Persian monarchs; Ezra 7:12 has Artaxerxes use it of himself and Daniel 2:37 applies it to Nebuchadnezzar. Deuteronomy 10:17 and Psalm 136:2-3 give the corresponding title to God. Verse 16 has it written on the robe and on the thigh, the place a rider's name would be visible to anyone standing beside the horse.

translationNotes.term: The marriage supper of the Lamb
translationNotes.original: Greek: τὸ δεῖπνον τοῦ γάμου τοῦ ἀρνίου (to deipnon tou gamou tou arniou)
translationNotes.note: A Jewish wedding ran in two stages: the betrothal, legally binding from the day it was made, and later the procession that brought the bride to the groom's house for a feast lasting days. Verse 9 pronounces a blessing on those invited to that supper. Verses 17-18 immediately set a second supper against it, the one the birds are called to.

stories.keyTakeaway: Heaven erupts in praise as God judges the great prostitute, and a wedding supper for the Lamb is announced; then a rider on a white horse called Faithful and True wages war against the beast and kings of the earth, capturing the beast and false prophet while his armies are defeated by the sword from his mouth.

headings.text: The Rider on the White Horse
Defeat of the Beast and False Prophet

stories.title: 🕊️ Revelation 20
summaryBullets: Then I saw an angel coming down from heaven with the key to the Abyss, holding in his hand a great chain. (20:1).
He seized the dragon, that ancient serpent who is the devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years. (20:2).

And he threw him into the Abyss, shut it, and sealed it over him, so that he could not deceive the nations until the thousand years were complete. After that, he must be released for a brief period of time. (20:3).

Then I saw the thrones, and those seated on them had been given authority to judge. And I saw the souls of those who had been beheaded for their testimony of Jesus and for the word of God, and those who had not worshiped the beast or its image and had not received its mark on their foreheads or hands. And they came to life and reigned with Christ for a thousand years. (20:4).
The rest of the dead did not come back to life until the thousand years were complete. This is the first resurrection. (20:5).

Blessed and holy are those who share in the first resurrection! The second death has no power over them, but they will be priests of God and of Christ and will reign with Him for a thousand years. (20:6).
When the thousand years are complete, Satan will be released from his prison, (20:7).
and will go out to deceive the nations in the four corners of the earth — Gog and Magog — to assemble them for battle. Their number is like the sand of the seashore. (20:8).
And they marched across the broad expanse of the earth and surrounded the camp of the saints and the beloved city. But fire came down from heaven and consumed them. (20:9).

And the devil who had deceived them was thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur, into which the beast and the false prophet had already been thrown. There they will be tormented day and night forever and ever. (20:10).
Then I saw a great white throne and the One seated on it. Earth and heaven fled from His presence, and no place was found for them. (20:11).

And I saw the dead, great and small, standing before the throne. And books were opened, and one of them was the Book of Life. And the dead were judged according to their deeds, as recorded in the books. (20:12).
The sea gave up its dead, and Death and Hades gave up their dead, and each one was judged according to his deeds. (20:13).
Then Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death — the lake of fire. (20:14).
And if anyone was found whose name was not written in the Book of Life, he was thrown into the lake of fire. (20:15).
crossRefs: Ezekiel 38:2: Gog of Magog prophecy.
Luke 10:20: Names written in heaven.
Daniel 7:22: Judgment given to saints.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֶלֶף שָׁנִים (ʾelef šānîm), Greek: χίλια ἔτη (chília étē, NT), Aramaic: אלפא שנין (ʾalpā šnīn)
translationNotes.note: A thousand-year period described here of Satan’s binding and saints’ reign; only occurs in Revelation 20.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: תְּהוֹם (təhom, sense), Greek: ἄβυσσος (ábyssos, NT), Aramaic: תְּהוֹמָא (təhomā)
translationNotes.note: The deep or bottomless pit; place of confinement for Satan.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הַתְּחִיָּה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה (hatəḥiyyāh harīʾshonāh, sense), Greek: ἡ ἀνάστασις ἡ πρώτη (hē anástasis hē prōtē, NT), Aramaic: קיָמא קדמָאה (qayyāmā qadmayā)
translationNotes.note: Rising of the martyrs and faithful to reign with Christ for a thousand years.

stories.title: 🕊️ Revelation 21
summaryBullets: Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and earth had passed away, and the sea was no more. (21:1).
I saw the holy city, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. (21:2).

And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying: “Behold, the dwelling place of God is with man, and He will dwell with them. They will be His people, and God Himself will be with them as their God. (21:3).
‘He will wipe away every tear from their eyes,’ and there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the former things have passed away.” (21:4).
And the One seated on the throne said, “Behold, I make all things new.” Then He said, “Write this down, for these words are faithful and true.” (21:5).
And He told me, “It is done! I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End. To the thirsty I will give freely from the spring of the water of life. (21:6).
The one who overcomes will inherit all things, and I will be his God, and he will be My son. (21:7).

But to the cowardly and unbelieving and abominable and murderers and sexually immoral and sorcerers and idolaters and all liars, their place will be in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur. This is the second death.” (21:8).
Then one of the seven angels with the seven bowls full of the seven final plagues came and said to me, “Come, I will show you the bride, the wife of the Lamb.” (21:9).
And he carried me away in the Spirit to a mountain great and high, and showed me the holy city of Jerusalem coming down out of heaven from God, (21:10).
shining with the glory of God. Its radiance was like a most precious jewel, like a jasper, as clear as crystal. (21:11).
The city had a great and high wall with twelve gates inscribed with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel, and twelve angels at the gates. (21:12).
There were three gates on the east, three on the north, three on the south, and three on the west. (21:13).
The wall of the city had twelve foundations bearing the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb. (21:14).
The angel who spoke with me had a golden measuring rod to measure the city and its gates and walls. (21:15).
The city lies foursquare, with its width the same as its length. And he measured the city with the rod, and all its dimensions were equal — 12,000 stadia in length and width and height. (21:16).
And he measured its wall to be 144 cubits, by the human measure the angel was using. (21:17).
The wall was made of jasper, and the city itself of pure gold, as pure as glass. (21:18).
The foundations of the city walls were adorned with every kind of precious stone: The first foundation was jasper, the second sapphire, the third chalcedony, the fourth emerald, (21:19).
the fifth sardonyx, the sixth carnelian, the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase, the eleventh jacinth, and the twelfth amethyst. (21:20).
And the twelve gates were twelve pearls, with each gate consisting of a single pearl. The main street of the city was pure gold, as clear as glass. (21:21).
But I saw no temple in the city, because the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple. (21:22).
And the city has no need of sun or moon to shine on it, because the glory of God illuminates the city, and the Lamb is its lamp. (21:23).
By its light the nations will walk, and into it the kings of the earth will bring their glory. (21:24).
Its gates will never be shut at the end of the day, because there will be no night there. (21:25).
And into the city will be brought the glory and honor of the nations. (21:26).
But nothing unclean will ever enter it, nor anyone who practices an abomination or a lie, but only those whose names are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life. (21:27).
crossRefs: Isaiah 65:17-19: I create new heavens and a new earth, and the sound of weeping shall no more be heard in her.
Isaiah 25:6-8: He will swallow up death forever and wipe away tears from all faces, and take away His people's reproach.
Isaiah 54:11-12: I will set your stones in antimony, your foundations in sapphires, and your gates of carbuncles.
Ezekiel 48:30-35: The city's twelve gates are named for the twelve tribes, three on each of its four sides.
Exodus 28:15-21: Four rows of three stones on the high priest's breastpiece, each engraved with the name of a tribe.

translationNotes.original: Greek: σταδίων δώδεκα χιλιάδων (stadion dodeka chiliadon)
translationNotes.note: A stadion is about 607 feet, 185 metres, so twelve thousand of them come to roughly 1,380 miles, 2,220 kilometres. Verse 16 says the city is laid out as a square with its length, breadth and height equal, so it is as tall as it is wide. For scale, that footprint would cover most of the Roman empire from Britain to Egypt.

translationNotes.original: Greek: πηχῶν ἑκατὸν τεσσεράκοντα τεσσάρων (pechon hekaton tesserakonta tessaron)
translationNotes.note: A cubit is about eighteen inches, forearm length, so the wall in 21:17 measures about 216 feet, 66 metres. The verse adds that this is a human measurement, which the angel was using. Twelve times twelve, like the twelve gates, the twelve foundations and the twelve thousand stadia.

translationNotes.original: Greek: μέτρον κάλαμον χρυσοῦν (metron kalamon chrysoun, a golden reed for measuring)
translationNotes.note: A kalamos is a reed, and a cut reed of a standard length was the ordinary surveyor's rod of the ancient Near East. Ezekiel 40:3 has a man with a linen cord and a measuring reed doing the same job around a temple, and Zechariah 2:1-2 has a man going out with a measuring line to measure Jerusalem. Measuring a thing was a way of laying claim to it.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἴασπις, σάπφειρος, χαλκηδών, σμάραγδος (iaspis, sappheiros, chalkedon, smaragdos)
translationNotes.note: Ancient stone names do not line up with modern mineralogy. What the Greeks called sapphiros was almost certainly lapis lazuli, deep blue flecked with gold-coloured pyrite, and their topazion was probably the yellow-green stone now called peridot; jacinth was a blue stone. Pliny the Elder's Natural History book 37 is the ancient catalogue these names come from. The list of twelve deliberately echoes the twelve stones on the high priest's breastpiece (Exodus 28:17-20).

translationNotes.original: Greek: μαργαρίτης (margarites, pearl)
translationNotes.note: Pearls were the most valuable single objects in the Roman luxury market, above gold by weight. Pliny reports that Cleopatra owned a pearl valued at ten million sesterces and that the two she owned were the largest known (Natural History 9.119-121). Verse 21 says each of the twelve gates was one pearl, and that gate had to admit a wall two hundred feet high.

translationNotes.original: Greek: Ἰερουσαλὴμ καινή (Ierousalem kaine)
translationNotes.note: The adjective is kainos, new in kind rather than merely recent. The city comes down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband (21:2), which is the reverse direction from every tower men build in Scripture. Verse 22 records what it does not contain: no temple, because the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple.

translationNotes.original: Greek: δωρεάν (dorean, as a gift, free of charge)
translationNotes.note: Dorean is the commercial word for something handed over with no price attached. It is what Jesus says of what the disciples received and must give (Matthew 10:8), and what Paul means by being justified as a gift (Romans 3:24). Verse 6 gives the water of life dorean to the thirsty, which is Isaiah 55:1 in Greek: come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.

stories.keyTakeaway: John sees a new heaven and earth with the Holy City, the new Jerusalem, descending from God; it is a square city 12,000 stadia on each side, built of gold and precious stones with twelve gates and foundations inscribed with the names of Israel's tribes and the apostles. God dwells among the people, wipes away all tears and pain, and the victorious inherit this city while the cowardly and unbelieving are consigned to the lake of burning sulfur.

stories.title: 📜 Revelation 22
summaryBullets: Then the angel showed me a river of the water of life, as clear as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb (22:1).

down the middle of the main street of the city. On either side of the river stood a tree of life, bearing twelve kinds of fruit and yielding a fresh crop for each month. And the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations. (22:2).
No longer will there be any curse. The throne of God and of the Lamb will be within the city, and His servants will worship Him. (22:3).
They will see His face, and His name will be on their foreheads. (22:4).
There will be no more night in the city, and they will have no need for the light of a lamp or of the sun. For the Lord God will shine on them, and they will reign forever and ever. (22:5).
Then the angel said to me, “These words are faithful and true. The Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets, has sent His angel to show His servants what must soon take place.” (22:6).
[J]“Behold, I am coming soon. Blessed is the one who keeps the words of prophecy in this book.”[/J] (22:7).
And I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things. And when I had heard and seen them, I fell down to worship at the feet of the angel who had shown me these things. (22:8).
But he said to me, “Do not do that! I am a fellow servant with you and your brothers the prophets, and with those who keep the words of this book. Worship God!” (22:9).
Then he told me, “Do not seal up the words of prophecy in this book, because the time is near. (22:10).
Let the unrighteous continue to be unrighteous, and the vile continue to be vile; let the righteous continue to practice righteousness, and the holy continue to be holy.” (22:11).
[J]“Behold, I am coming soon, and My reward is with Me, to give to each one according to what he has done.[/J] (22:12).
[J]I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End.”[/J] (22:13).
[J]Blessed are those who wash their robes, so that they may have the right to the tree of life and may enter the city by its gates.[/J] (22:14).
[J]But outside are the dogs, the sorcerers, the sexually immoral, the murderers, the idolaters, and everyone who loves and practices falsehood.[/J] (22:15).
[J]“I, Jesus, have sent My angel to give you this testimony for the churches. I am the Root and the Offspring of David, the bright Morning Star.”[/J] (22:16).
The Spirit and the bride say, “Come!” Let the one who hears say, “Come!” And let the one who is thirsty come, and the one who desires the water of life drink freely. (22:17).
I testify to everyone who hears the words of prophecy in this book: If anyone adds to them, God will add to him the plagues described in this book. (22:18).
And if anyone takes away from the words of this book of prophecy, God will take away his share in the tree of life and the holy city, which are described in this book. (22:19).
He who testifies to these things says, [J]“Yes, I am coming soon.”[/J] Amen. Come, Lord Jesus! (22:20).
The grace of the Lord Jesus be with all the saints. Amen. (22:21).
crossRefs: Genesis 3:22-24: The way to the tree of life is guarded by cherubim and a flaming sword turning every way.
Ezekiel 47:1-12: Water flows from under the temple threshold, and trees on both banks bear fruit every month, their leaves for healing.
Zechariah 14:8-11: Living waters flow out from Jerusalem summer and winter, and there shall be no more curse.
Daniel 12:4-10: Daniel is told to shut up the words and seal the book until the time of the end.
Deuteronomy 4:1-2: Do not add to the word I command you, and do not take anything from it.

translationNotes.term: The river and the tree of life
translationNotes.original: Greek: ξύλον ζωῆς (xylon zoes, tree of life)
translationNotes.note: A river flows from the throne down the middle of the street, with the tree on both sides bearing twelve crops, one each month, its leaves for the healing of the nations (22:1-2). Ezekiel 47:1-12 describes water from under the temple threshold with trees on both banks fruiting monthly and leaves for healing. The tree first appears in Genesis 2:9 and was closed off in Genesis 3:22-24; here the guard is gone.

translationNotes.term: Do not seal up the words
translationNotes.original: Greek: μὴ σφραγίσῃς τοὺς λόγους (me sphragises tous logous)
translationNotes.note: Daniel was told the opposite: shut up the words and seal the book until the time of the end (Daniel 12:4, 9). Sealing a document kept it closed and unread until the right moment. The instruction in 22:10 is that this scroll is not to be sealed, because the time is near.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἐπιθῇ ἐπ' αὐτά (epithe ep' auta, if anyone adds to them)
translationNotes.note: The warning in 22:18-19 is the same formula Moses uses twice, do not add to the word and do not take from it (Deuteronomy 4:2; 12:32). Ancient treaties and public documents commonly carried a clause of this kind to stop copyists and officials from altering the text. Here it closes the book it belongs to.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἔρχου κύριε Ἰησοῦ (erchou kyrie Iesou) - Aramaic: מרנא תא (marana tha, our Lord, come)
translationNotes.note: The prayer in 22:20 is preserved in its Aramaic form by Paul at the end of 1 Corinthians, marana tha (1 Corinthians 16:22), and the Didache, an early church manual, uses the same Aramaic word in a communion prayer. Aramaic was the everyday language of Judea, so this is one of the few places where the actual sound of the earliest believers' prayer survives in the text.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ὁ ἀστὴρ ὁ λαμπρὸς ὁ πρωϊνός (ho aster ho lampros ho proinos)
translationNotes.note: The morning star is the planet Venus, the last light still visible as the sky goes grey, the sign that night is ending. Balaam's oracle says a star shall come out of Jacob and a sceptre rise out of Israel (Numbers 24:17), and 2 Peter 1:19 speaks of the morning star rising in your hearts. In 22:16 Jesus applies the title to Himself, along with the root and the offspring of David.

translationNotes.original: Greek: λατρεύω (latreuo)
translationNotes.note: Latreuo means to serve or minister, especially in priestly duty, and it is the word behind English liturgy's companion term latria. Luke 1:74-75 uses it of serving God in holiness all our days, and Paul applies it in Romans 12:1 to presenting your body as a living sacrifice. Revelation 22:3 says His servants will latreuo Him and see His face, which is temple language for work, not for a posture.

stories.keyTakeaway: The angel shows John the river of life, tree of life, and throne of God in the holy city where God's servants will serve him and see his face; Jesus declares he is coming soon and warns against adding to or removing words from this prophecy.

headings.text: Nothing May Be Added or Removed

intro:
Revelation was written by John the apostle, son of Zebedee and Salome, originally a fisherman from Bethsaida on the Sea of Galilee and the younger brother of the apostle James. Early church tradition from the second century AD (Justin Martyr, Irenaeus, Tertullian) identifies the author of Revelation as this John. According to Tertullian, John was banished to Patmos by Roman authorities after surviving an attempt to execute him by boiling in oil in Rome. The writing dates to around AD 95, the closing years of the emperor Domitian's reign (81-96 AD), and was composed during John's exile on Patmos, a small island in the Aegean Sea off the western coast of Asia Minor. After Domitian's assassination in AD 96, John was released and returned to Ephesus, where he had ministered following the destruction of Jerusalem in AD 70 and where he is said to have lived into old age and died around AD 100. The historical setting is the height of the Roman Empire under the Flavian dynasty; Domitian had reorganized the imperial cult, demanded the title "Dominus et Deus" (Lord and God), and Roman authorities had begun enforcing emperor worship across the empire. Believers who refused to acknowledge Caesar as lord were facing exile, confiscation of property, and execution.

Revelation is the twenty-seventh and final book of the New Testament. The Greek title Apokalypsis means "unveiling" or "uncovering," from the opening words of the book ("Apokalypsis Iesou Christou," "Revelation of Jesus Christ"). The earliest substantial surviving manuscript of Revelation is Papyrus 47 (Chester Beatty III), dated to around 200-250 AD and housed at the Chester Beatty Library in Dublin; the earliest complete copy is Codex Sinaiticus, dated to the 4th century AD.
